title.zh: 卷四百二十八 列傳第一百八十七 道學二 程氏門人 劉絢 李籲 謝良佐 游酢 張繹 蘇昞 尹焞 楊時 羅從彥 李侗
title.en: Volume 428 Biographies 187: Taoist Scholars 2 - Cheng Shimenren, Liu Xuan, Li Yu, Xie Liangzuo, You Cu, Zhang Yi, Su Bing, Yin Tun, Yang Shi, Luo Congyan, Li Tong
title.raw: 卷四百二十八 列傳第一百八十七 道學二 程氏門人 劉絢 李籲 謝良佐 游酢 張繹 蘇昞 尹焞 楊時 羅從彥 李侗 Volume 428 Biographies 187: Taoist Scholars 2 - Cheng Shimenren, Liu Xuan, Li Yu, Xie Liangzuo, You Cu, Zhang Yi, Su Bing, Yin Tun, Yang Shi, Luo Congyan, Li Tong

sentences.zh: 劉絢 李吁 謝良佐 游酢 張繹 蘇昺 尹焞 楊時 羅從彥 李侗

translations.literal: Liu Xuan, Li Yu, Xie Liangzuo, You Zuo, Zhang Yi, Su Bing, Yin Tun, Yang Shi, Luo Congyan, Li Tong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, Li Yu, Xie Liangzuo, You Zuo, Zhang Yi, Su Bing, Yin Tun, Yang Shi, Luo Congyan, and Li Tong

sentences.zh: 劉絢字質夫，常山人。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan, courtesy name Zhifu, was a man of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, styled Zhifu, was a native of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 以蔭為壽安主簿、長子令，督公家逋賦，不假鞭撲而集。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he served as Chief Clerk of Shou'an and Magistrate of Changzi; when supervising government tax arrears, he collected them without resorting to whipping and beating.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he was appointed chief clerk of Shou'an and magistrate of Changzi; when he collected overdue public taxes, he did so without recourse to the lash.

sentences.zh: 歲大旱，府遣吏視傷所，蠲財什二，絢力爭不得，封還其楬，請易之。

translations.literal: In a year of great drought, the prefecture sent an official to inspect disaster areas and remitted two-tenths of taxes; Xuan strove in vain to change this, sealed and returned the edict, and requested a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought, the prefecture dispatched an official to assess the damage and remitted two-tenths of the tax levy. Xuan argued strenuously but could not prevail; he sealed and returned the proclamation and asked that it be replaced.

sentences.zh: 富弼歎曰：「真縣令也。」

translations.literal: Fu Bi sighed and said: "A true magistrate."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi sighed and said, "There is a true magistrate."

sentences.zh: 元祐初，韓維薦其經明行修，為京兆府教授。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, Han Wei recommended him for mastery of the classics and upright conduct, and he was appointed professor in the Jingzhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanyou reign, Han Wei recommended him for classical learning and exemplary conduct, and he was made professor in the Jingzhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王巖叟、朱光庭又薦為太學博士，卒於官。

translations.literal: Wang Yansou and Zhu Guangting further recommended him as Erudite of the Imperial Academy, and he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansou and Zhu Guangting also recommended him for the post of Erudite at the Imperial Academy; he died while holding office.

sentences.zh: 絢力學不倦，最明於《春秋》。

translations.literal: Xuan studied tirelessly and was most accomplished in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan pursued learning without weariness and was especially accomplished in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 程顥每為人言：「他人之學，敏則有矣，未易保也，若絢者，吾無疑焉。」

translations.literal: Cheng Hao often said to others: "Other men's learning may be quick, but it is not easy to preserve; as for one like Xuan, I have no doubts."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hao often told others, "Other men's learning may be quick enough, but it is not easily sustained; as for someone like Xuan, I have no doubts about him."

sentences.zh: 李吁字端伯，洛陽人。

translations.literal: Li Yu, courtesy name Duanbo, was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, styled Duanbo, was a native of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 元祐中為秘書省校書郎，卒。

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou era he served as Collator of the Secretariat, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era he served as collator in the Secretariat and then died.

sentences.zh: 程頤謂其才器可以大受，及亡也，祭之以文曰：「自予兄弟倡明道學，能使學者視仿而信從者，吁與劉絢有焉。」

translations.literal: Cheng Yi said his talent and capacity could bear great things; when he died, Yi eulogized him in writing, saying: "Since my brother and I first advocated the learning of the Way, those who could make scholars look to them and follow in faith were Yu and Liu Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi said his talent and capacity were fit for great things. When Yu died, Yi wrote a funeral eulogy saying, "Since my brother and I first advocated the learning of the Way, those who could make scholars look to them and follow in faith were Yu and Liu Xuan."

sentences.zh: 謝良佐

translations.literal: Xie Liangzuo
translations.idiomatic: Xie Liangzuo

sentences.zh: 謝良佐字顯道，壽春上蔡人。

translations.literal: Xie Liangzuo, courtesy name Xiandao, was a man of Shangcai in Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Liangzuo, styled Xiandao, was a native of Shangcai in Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 與游酢、呂大臨、楊時在程門，號「四先生」。

translations.literal: Together with You Zuo, Lü Dalin, and Yang Shi he studied under the Cheng school and was called one of the "Four Masters."
translations.idiomatic: Together with You Zuo, Lü Dalin, and Yang Shi he studied under the Cheng school and was known as one of the "Four Masters."

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國初，官京師，召對，忤旨去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong Jingguo era he held office in the capital, was summoned for an audience, offended the throne, and left.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianzhong Jingguo era he held office in the capital, was summoned for an audience, ran afoul of the throne, and departed.

sentences.zh: 監西京竹木場，坐口語系詔獄，廢為民。

translations.literal: He supervised the bamboo and timber depot of the Western Capital; because of spoken words he was imprisoned by imperial edict and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: He served as supervisor of the bamboo and timber depot at the Western Capital; for words he had spoken he was imprisoned by imperial order and stripped of office, reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 良佐記問該贍，對人稱引前史，至不差一字。

translations.literal: Liangzuo's memory and learning were comprehensive; when citing earlier histories to others, he did not miss a single character.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo's memory and erudition were comprehensive; when he quoted earlier histories to others, he never missed a single character.

sentences.zh: 事有未徹，則顙有泚。

translations.literal: When a matter was not fully understood, sweat would appear on his forehead.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a matter was not fully understood, sweat would bead on his forehead.

sentences.zh: 與程頤別一年，復來見，問其所進，曰：「但去得一『矜』字爾。」

translations.literal: After parting from Cheng Yi for a year, he came to see him again; asked what progress he had made, he said: "I have merely removed one word—'pride.'"
translations.idiomatic: After a year's separation from Cheng Yi, he came to see him again. When asked what progress he had made, he said, "I have merely done away with one word—'pride.'"

sentences.zh: 頤喜，謂朱光庭曰：「是子力學，切問而近思者也。」

translations.literal: Yi was pleased and said to Zhu Guangting: "This young man studies hard; he asks earnestly and thinks close at hand."
translations.idiomatic: Yi was pleased and said to Zhu Guangting, "This young man studies diligently; he asks earnestly and reflects on what is near at hand."

sentences.zh: 所著《論語說》行於世。

translations.literal: His Exposition of the Analects circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Exposition of the Analects circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 游酢字定夫，建州建陽人。

translations.literal: You Zuo, courtesy name Dingfu, was a man of Jianyang in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: You Zuo, styled Dingfu, was a native of Jianyang in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 與兄醇以文行知名，所交皆天下士。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Chun were renowned for literary accomplishment and conduct; those they befriended were all eminent men under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Chun were renowned for literary accomplishment and upright conduct; their associates were all eminent scholars of the realm.

sentences.zh: 程頤見之京師，謂其資可以進道。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi met him in the capital and said his endowment could advance in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi met him in the capital and said his native endowment was suited to progress in the Way.

sentences.zh: 程顥興扶溝學，招使肄業，盡棄其學而學焉。

translations.literal: Cheng Hao established the Fugou academy and invited him to study there; he abandoned his previous learning entirely and studied under Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Hao founded the academy at Fugou and invited him to study there, he abandoned his previous learning entirely and devoted himself to Hao's teaching.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調蕭山尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as magistrate of Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 近臣薦其賢，召為太學錄。

translations.literal: A court intimate recommended his worth, and he was summoned to serve as Recorder of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A court intimate recommended his virtue, and he was summoned to serve as recorder of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 遷博士，以奉親不便，求知河清縣。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Erudite, but because serving his parents was inconvenient, he requested appointment as magistrate of Heqing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Erudite, but because the post made it difficult to care for his parents, he requested appointment as magistrate of Heqing County.

sentences.zh: 范純仁守穎昌府，辟府教授。

translations.literal: When Fan Chunren served as prefect of Yingchang, he recruited Zuo as professor of the prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Chunren served as prefect of Yingchang, he recruited Zuo as professor of the prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 純仁入相，復為博士。

translations.literal: When Chunren entered the chancellorship, Zuo again became an Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunren entered the chancellorship, Zuo again became an Erudite at the academy.

sentences.zh: 簽書齊州、泉州判官。

translations.literal: He served as signing secretary and judicial administrator of Qizhou and Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as signing secretary and judicial administrator in Qizhou and Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 晚得監察御史，歷知漢陽軍、和舒濠三州而卒。

translations.literal: Late in life he obtained the post of Supervising Censor and successively served as prefect of Hanyang, He, Shu, and Hao before dying.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he obtained the post of supervising censor and successively governed Hanyang, He, Shu, and Hao before he died.

sentences.zh: 張繹字思叔，河南壽安人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Sishu, was a man of Shou'an in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, styled Sishu, was a native of Shou'an in Henan.

sentences.zh: 家甚微，年長未知學，傭力於市，出聞邑官傳呼聲，心慕之，問人曰：「何以得此？」

translations.literal: His family was very poor; when he was grown he still did not know learning and hired out his labor in the market. Going out, he heard the calling voice of the county official and admired it in his heart; he asked someone: "How does one obtain this?"
translations.idiomatic: His family was very poor. Though already grown, he had not yet begun to study and hired out his labor in the market. One day he went out and heard a county official's attendants calling ahead; he admired this and asked someone, "How does one obtain such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 人曰：「此讀書所致爾。」

translations.literal: The man said: "This comes from reading books, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The man replied, "That comes from reading books, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 即發憤力學，遂以文名。

translations.literal: Thereupon he resolved himself and studied hard, and soon became renowned for letters.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he resolved himself and studied hard, and soon became renowned for his literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 預鄉里計偕，謂科舉之習不足為，嘗游僧捨，見僧道楷，將祝髮從之。

translations.literal: When he joined the local examination caravan, he considered the habits of the examination system unworthy of pursuit; once while visiting a monk's quarters he saw the monk Daokai and was about to shave his head and follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When he joined the local examination caravan, he decided the habits of the examination system were not worth pursuing. Once, while visiting a monastery, he saw the monk Daokai and was about to shave his head and become his disciple.

sentences.zh: 時周行己官河南，警之曰：「何為捨聖人之學而學佛？

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Xingji held office in Henan and warned him, saying: "Why abandon the learning of the sages to study Buddhism?
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhou Xingji held office in Henan and warned him, "Why abandon the learning of the sages to study Buddhism?

sentences.zh: 異日程先生歸，可師也。」

translations.literal: Before long Master Cheng will return; you may take him as your teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Master Cheng will return; you may take him as your teacher."

sentences.zh: 會程頤還自涪，乃往受業，頤賞其穎悟。

translations.literal: It happened that Cheng Yi returned from Fu, whereupon he went to receive instruction; Yi admired his quick understanding.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Yi returned from Fu, he went to receive instruction under him, and Yi admired his quick understanding.

sentences.zh: 讀《孟子》「志士不忘在溝壑，勇士不忘喪其元」，慨然若有得。

translations.literal: Reading in the Mencius, "A man of purpose does not forget that he may end in ditches and gullies; a brave man does not forget that he may lose his head," he was moved as though he had gained something.
translations.idiomatic: Reading in the Mencius the passage, "A man of purpose does not forget that he may end in ditches and gullies; a brave man does not forget that he may lose his head," he was deeply moved, as though he had gained something.

sentences.zh: 未及仕而卒。

translations.literal: Before he had entered office he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had entered office he died.

sentences.zh: 頤嘗言「吾晚得二士」，謂繹與尹焞也。

translations.literal: Yi once said, "Late in life I obtained two scholars," referring to Yi and Yin Tun.
translations.idiomatic: Yi once said, "Late in life I obtained two fine scholars," referring to Zhang Yi and Yin Tun.

sentences.zh: 蘇昺字季明，武功人。

translations.literal: Su Bing, courtesy name Jiming, was a man of Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Su Bing, styled Jiming, was a native of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 始學於張載，而事二程卒業。

translations.literal: He first studied under Zhang Zai, then completed his training under the two Chengs.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied under Zhang Zai and completed his training under the two Chengs.

sentences.zh: 元祐末，呂大中薦之，起布衣為太常博士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanyou era, Lü Dazhong recommended him, and he was raised from commoner status to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanyou era, Lü Dazhong recommended him, and he was raised from commoner status to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 坐元符上書入邪籍，編管饒州，卒。

translations.literal: Because of a memorial submitted during the Yuanfu era he was entered on the heterodox register, was banished under guard to Raozhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a memorial he submitted during the Yuanfu era he was entered on the heterodox register, banished under guard to Raozhou, and died there.

sentences.zh: 尹焞字彥明，一字德充，世為洛人。

translations.literal: Yin Tun, courtesy name Yanming, also styled Dechong, was for generations a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Tun, styled Yanming and also known as Dechong, came from a Luoyang family of long standing.

sentences.zh: 曾祖仲宣七子，而二子有名：長子源字子漸，是謂河內先生；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhongxuan had seven sons, of whom two became famous: the eldest, Yuan, courtesy name Zijian, was called Master Henei;
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhongxuan had seven sons, of whom two became famous: the eldest, Yuan, styled Zijian, was known as Master Henei;

sentences.zh: 次子洙字師魯，是謂河南先生。

translations.literal: the second, Zhu, courtesy name Shilu, was called Master Henan.
translations.idiomatic: the second, Zhu, styled Shilu, was known as Master Henan.

sentences.zh: 源生林，官至虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Yuan begot Lin, who reached the office of Vice Director of the Bureau of Forestry and Crafts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan begot Lin, who rose to the post of vice director of the Bureau of Forestry and Crafts.

sentences.zh: 林生焞。

translations.literal: Lin begot Tun.
translations.idiomatic: Lin begot Tun.

sentences.zh: 少師事程頤，嘗應舉，發策有誅元祐諸臣議，焞曰：「噫，尚可以干祿乎哉！」

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Cheng Yi. Once he took the examination; the essay topic proposed punishing the officials of the Yuanyou faction. Tun said: "Alas! Can one still seek official emolument?"
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Cheng Yi. Once he took the examination and encountered an essay topic proposing punishment for the officials of the Yuanyou faction. Tun said, "Alas! Is it still fitting to seek office and emolument?"

sentences.zh: 不對而出，告頤曰：「焞不復應進士舉矣。」

translations.literal: He did not answer and left, telling Yi: "Tun will no longer take the jinshi examination."
translations.idiomatic: He refused to answer and left, telling Yi, "Tun will no longer take the jinshi examination."

sentences.zh: 頤曰：「子有母在。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "You still have your mother living."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "You still have your mother to support."

sentences.zh: □享歸告其母陳，母曰：「吾知汝以善養，不知汝以祿養。」

translations.literal: Tun returned home and told his mother Chen; his mother said: "I know you would support me through virtue; I did not know you would support me through official emolument."
translations.idiomatic: Tun returned home and told his mother Chen. His mother said, "I know you would support me through virtue; I did not know you would support me through official salary."

sentences.zh: 頤聞之曰：「賢哉母也！」

translations.literal: When Yi heard of this he said: "What a worthy mother!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yi heard of this he said, "What a worthy mother!"

sentences.zh: 於是終身不就舉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he never again took the examination for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he never again took the examination for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 焞之從師，與河南張繹同時，繹以高識，焞以篤行。

translations.literal: When Tun studied under his teacher, he did so at the same time as Zhang Yi of Henan; Yi was noted for lofty insight, Tun for steadfast conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Tun studied under his teacher at the same time as Zhang Yi of Henan; Yi was noted for lofty insight, Tun for steadfast conduct.

sentences.zh: 頤既沒，焞聚從洛中，非弔喪問疾不出戶，士大夫宗仰之。

translations.literal: After Yi died, Tun gathered fellow disciples in Luoyang and did not leave his door except to attend funerals or visit the sick; scholar-officials looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi died, Tun gathered with fellow disciples in Luoyang and did not leave his home except to attend funerals or visit the sick; scholar-officials revered him.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，種師道薦焞德行可備勸講，召至京師，不欲留，賜號和靖處士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, Zhong Shidao recommended Tun's virtue and conduct as fit for exhortation and lecturing; he was summoned to the capital, did not wish to remain, and was granted the title Reclusive Gentleman of Hejing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingkang era, Zhong Shidao recommended Tun's virtue and conduct as fit for exhortation and lecturing. He was summoned to the capital but did not wish to remain and was granted the title Reclusive Gentleman of Hejing.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書梅執禮、御史中丞呂好問、戶部侍郎邵溥、中書舍人胡安國合奏：「河南布衣尹焞學窮根本，德備中和，言動可以師法，器識可以任大，近世招延之士無出其右者。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Mei Zhili, Censor-in-Chief Lü Haowen, Vice Minister of Revenue Shao Pu, and Drafting Attendant Hu Anguo jointly memorialized: "The commoner Yin Tun of Henan has exhausted the roots of learning, his virtue fulfills the Mean, his words and conduct may serve as models, and his capacity and insight can bear great responsibility; among those recruited in recent times, none surpasses him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Mei Zhili, Censor-in-Chief Lü Haowen, Vice Minister of Revenue Shao Pu, and Drafting Attendant Hu Anguo jointly memorialized, "The commoner Yin Tun of Henan has mastered learning to its roots, his virtue fulfills the Mean, his words and conduct may serve as models, and his capacity and insight can bear great responsibility; among those recruited in recent times, none surpasses him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷特召，而命處士以歸，使焞韜藏國器，不為時用，未副陛下側席求賢之意。

translations.literal: The court specially summoned him, yet ordered the reclusive gentleman to return home, causing Tun to hide away the state's vessels and not be employed by the age—this fails to accord with Your Majesty's intent of leaving one's seat to seek the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The court specially summoned him, yet ordered the reclusive gentleman to return home, leaving Tun to conceal his talents for the state and go unused by the age—this does not fulfill Your Majesty's intent of leaving your seat to seek the worthy.

sentences.zh: 望特加識擢，以慰士大夫之望。」

translations.literal: We hope he may be specially recognized and promoted, to satisfy the hopes of scholar-officials."
translations.idiomatic: We hope he may be specially recognized and promoted, to satisfy the hopes of scholar-officials."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: There was no response.

sentences.zh: 次年，金人陷洛，焞闔門被害，焞死復甦，門人舁置山谷中而免。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Jurchens took Luoyang, Tun's entire household was attacked; Tun died and revived, and his disciples carried him to a mountain valley and thus he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Jurchens took Luoyang, Tun's entire household was attacked. Tun died and revived, and his disciples carried him to a mountain valley, where he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 劉豫命偽帥趙斌以禮聘焞，不從則以兵恐之。

translations.literal: Liu Yu ordered the puppet commander Zhao Bin to invite Tun with ceremony; if he did not comply, he was to be threatened with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu ordered the puppet commander Zhao Bin to invite Tun with ceremony; if he refused, he was to be threatened with force.

sentences.zh: 焞自商州奔蜀，至閬，得程頤《易傳》十卦於其門人呂稽中，又得全本於其婿邢純，拜而受之。

translations.literal: Tun fled from Shangzhou to Shu; reaching Lang, he obtained ten hexagrams of Cheng Yi's Commentary on the Changes from his disciple Lü Jizhong, and also obtained the complete text from his son-in-law Xing Chun, receiving both with a bow.
translations.idiomatic: Tun fled from Shangzhou to Shu. Reaching Lang, he obtained ten hexagrams of Cheng Yi's Commentary on the Changes from his disciple Lü Jizhong, and also obtained the complete text from his son-in-law Xing Chun, receiving both with a bow.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，止於涪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, he stopped at Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, he settled at Fu.

sentences.zh: 涪，頤讀《易》地也，辟三畏齋以居，邦人不識其面。

translations.literal: Fu was where Yi had read the Changes; he opened the Three Reverences Studio to dwell there, and the people of the district did not know his face.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was where Yi had studied the Changes; he opened the Three Reverences Studio to live there, and the people of the district did not even know his face.

sentences.zh: 侍讀范沖舉焞自代，授左宣教郎，充崇政殿說書，以疾辭。

translations.literal: Reader-in-Waiting Fan Chong recommended Tun to replace him; Tun was appointed Left Instructor and Attendant Lecturer in the Chongzheng Hall, but declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-Waiting Fan Chong recommended Tun to replace him. Tun was appointed Left Instructor and attendant lecturer in the Chongzheng Hall, but declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 范沖奏給五百金為行資，遣漕臣奉詔至涪親遣。

translations.literal: Fan Chong memorialized to grant five hundred in gold as travel funds and dispatched a transport official bearing an edict to Fu to escort him in person.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chong memorialized to grant five hundred in gold as travel funds and dispatched a transport official bearing an edict to Fu to escort him in person.

sentences.zh: 六年，始就道，作文祭頤而後行。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he finally set out on the road, composing a text to sacrifice to Yi before departing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he finally set out on the road, composing a funeral text to sacrifice to Yi before departing.

sentences.zh: 先是，崇寧以來，禁錮元祐學術，高宗渡江，始召楊時置從班，召胡安國居給捨，范沖、朱震俱在講席，薦焞甚力。

translations.literal: Earlier, since the Chongning era, Yuanyou learning had been proscribed; when Gaozong crossed the Yangzi, Yang Shi was first summoned to the attendant ranks, Hu Anguo was summoned to the drafting office, Fan Chong and Zhu Zhen were both on the lecture seat, and they all recommended Tun with great force.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, since the Chongning era, Yuanyou learning had been proscribed. When Gaozong crossed the Yangzi, Yang Shi was first summoned to the attendant ranks, Hu Anguo was summoned to the drafting office, Fan Chong and Zhu Zhen were both on the lecture seat, and they all strongly recommended Tun.

sentences.zh: 既召，而左司諫公輔上疏攻程氏之學，乞加屏絕。

translations.literal: After the summons, Left Remonstrance Official Gong Fu submitted a memorial attacking the learning of the Cheng school and requesting that it be further proscribed.
translations.idiomatic: After the summons, Left Remonstrance Official Gong Fu submitted a memorial attacking the learning of the Cheng school and requesting that it be further proscribed.

sentences.zh: 焞至九江，上奏曰：「臣僚上言，程頤之學惑亂天下。

translations.literal: When Tun reached Jiujiang, he submitted a memorial saying: "Officials have stated above that Cheng Yi's learning has confused and disturbed all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Tun reached Jiujiang, he submitted a memorial saying, "Officials have stated above that Cheng Yi's learning has confused and disturbed all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 焞實師頤垂二十年，學之既專，自信甚篤。

translations.literal: Tun in truth studied under Yi for nearly twenty years; his learning was already specialized, and his self-confidence was very firm.
translations.idiomatic: Tun in truth studied under Yi for nearly twenty years; his learning was already specialized, and his conviction was very firm.

sentences.zh: 使焞濫列經筵，其所敷繹，不過聞於師者。

translations.literal: If Tun were improperly placed in the classics lecture seat, what he would expound would be nothing beyond what he heard from his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: If Tun were improperly placed in the classics lecture seat, what he would expound would be nothing beyond what he heard from his teacher.

sentences.zh: 捨其所學，是欺君父，加以疾病衰耗，不能支持。」

translations.literal: To abandon what he has learned would be to deceive his sovereign and father; moreover, illness and decline leave him unable to sustain the effort."
translations.idiomatic: To abandon what he has learned would be to deceive his sovereign and father; moreover, illness and decline leave him unable to sustain the effort."

sentences.zh: 遂留不進。

translations.literal: Thereupon he remained and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he remained and did not proceed to the capital.

sentences.zh: 胡安國奉祠居衡陽，上書言：「欲使學者蹈中庸，師孔、孟，而禁不從程頤之學，是入室而不由戶。」

translations.literal: Hu Anguo, holding a sacrificial stipend and dwelling in Hengyang, submitted a memorial saying: "To wish that scholars tread the Mean and take Confucius and Mencius as teachers, yet forbid them from following Cheng Yi's learning, is to enter a room without going through the door."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Anguo, holding a sacrificial stipend and dwelling in Hengyang, submitted a memorial saying, "To wish that scholars tread the Mean and take Confucius and Mencius as teachers, yet forbid them from following Cheng Yi's learning, is to enter a room without going through the door."

sentences.zh: 朱震引疾告去，時趙鼎去位，張浚獨相，於是召安國，俾以內祠兼侍讀，而上章薦焞，言其拒劉豫之節，且謂其所學所養有大過人者，乞令江州守臣疾速津送至國門。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhen cited illness and requested leave; at the time Zhao Ding had left office and Zhang Jun alone was chancellor. Thereupon Anguo was summoned and made to hold an inner sacrificial stipend while also serving as Reader; he submitted a memorial recommending Tun, speaking of his integrity in refusing Liu Yu, and stating that his learning and cultivation greatly surpassed others, requesting that the prefectural official of Jiangzhou be ordered to convey him swiftly by ferry to the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhen cited illness and requested leave. At the time Zhao Ding had left office and Zhang Jun alone was chancellor. Thereupon Anguo was summoned and made to hold an inner sacrificial stipend while also serving as reader; he submitted a memorial recommending Tun, speaking of his integrity in refusing Liu Yu, and stating that his learning and cultivation greatly surpassed others, requesting that the prefectural official of Jiangzhou be ordered to convey him swiftly by ferry to the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 復以疾辭，上曰：「焞可謂恬退矣。」

translations.literal: Again he declined on grounds of illness; the emperor said: "Tun may truly be called modest and retiring."
translations.idiomatic: Again he declined on grounds of illness. The emperor said, "Tun may truly be called modest and retiring."

sentences.zh: 詔以秘書郎兼說書，趣起之，焞始入見就職。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Secretary and Attendant Lecturer and urged him to take office; Tun then entered audience and assumed his post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him secretary and attendant lecturer and urged him to take office. Tun then entered audience and assumed his post.

sentences.zh: 八年，除秘書少監，未幾，力辭求去。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; before long he strenuously declined and requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat; before long he strenuously declined and requested leave.

sentences.zh: 上語參知政事劉大中曰：「焞未論所學淵源，足為後進矜式，班列得老成人，亦是朝廷氣象。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Vice Grand Councilor Liu Dazhong: "Setting aside the origins of Tun's learning, he is sufficient to serve as a model for later entrants; to have an elder of mature years in the ranks is also the bearing of the court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Vice Grand Councilor Liu Dazhong, "Setting aside the origins of Tun's learning, he is sufficient to serve as a model for later entrants; to have an elder of mature years in the ranks is also the bearing of the court."

sentences.zh: 乃以焞直徽猷閣，主管萬壽觀，留侍經筵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tun was made Direct Attendant of the Hall of Glorious Learning, put in charge of Wanshou Abbey, and retained to serve at the classics lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Tun was made direct attendant of the Hall of Glorious Learning, put in charge of Wanshou Abbey, and retained to serve at the classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 資善堂翊善朱震疾亟，薦焞自代。

translations.literal: Assistant Tutor Zhu Zhen of the Hall of Cultivating Virtue was gravely ill and recommended Tun to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Tutor Zhu Zhen of the Hall of Cultivating Virtue was gravely ill and recommended Tun to replace him.

sentences.zh: 輔臣入奏，上慘然曰：「楊時物故，胡安國與震又亡，朕痛惜之。」

translations.literal: The assisting ministers entered to report; the emperor said mournfully: "Yang Shi has passed away, and Hu Anguo and Zhen have also died; We grieve and regret this."
translations.idiomatic: The assisting ministers entered to report. The emperor said mournfully, "Yang Shi has passed away, and Hu Anguo and Zhen have also died; I grieve and regret this."

sentences.zh: 趙鼎曰：「尹焞學問淵源，可以繼震。」

translations.literal: Zhao Ding said: "Yin Tun's learning has deep origins and can succeed Zhen."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding said, "Yin Tun's learning has deep origins and can succeed Zhen."

sentences.zh: 上指奏牘曰：「震亦薦焞代資善之職，但焞微聵，恐教兒費力爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor pointed to the memorial and said: "Zhen also recommended Tun to replace him in the Hall of Cultivating Virtue, but Tun is slightly deaf; I fear teaching the children will be laborious."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pointed to the memorial and said, "Zhen also recommended Tun to replace him in the Hall of Cultivating Virtue, but Tun is slightly deaf; I fear teaching the children will be laborious."

sentences.zh: 除太常少卿，仍兼說書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while still concurrently serving as Attendant Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while still concurrently serving as attendant lecturer.

sentences.zh: 未幾，稱疾在告，除權禮部侍郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: Before long he reported illness and took leave; he was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Rites while concurrently serving as Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he reported illness and took leave; he was appointed acting vice minister of Rites while concurrently serving as lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 時金人遣張通古、蕭哲來議和，焞上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the time the Jurchens sent Zhang Tonggu and Xiao Zhe to negotiate peace; Tun submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jurchens sent Zhang Tonggu and Xiao Zhe to negotiate peace. Tun submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣伏見本朝有遼、金之禍，亙古未聞，中國無人，致其猾亂。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully observes that our dynasty has suffered the calamities of Liao and Jin, unheard of since antiquity; China had no men, and thus they grew crafty and rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully observes that our dynasty has suffered the calamities of Liao and Jin, unheard of since antiquity; China lacked capable men, and thus they grew crafty and rebellious.

sentences.zh: 昨者城下之戰，詭詐百出，二帝北狩，皇族播遷，宗社之危，已絕而續。

translations.literal: In the recent battle beneath the walls, stratagems and deceits appeared in every form; the two emperors went north on hunt, the imperial clan was scattered in exile, and the peril to altars and ancestral temples was cut off and then continued.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent battle beneath the walls, stratagems and deceits appeared in every form; the two emperors were taken north, the imperial clan was scattered in exile, and the peril to altars and ancestral temples was cut off and then continued.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來十有二年，雖中原未復，仇敵未殄，然而賴祖宗德澤之厚，陛下勤撫之至，億兆之心無有離異。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, twelve years have passed; although the Central Plain has not been recovered and the enemy has not been exterminated, yet relying on the thick virtue and grace of the ancestors and Your Majesty's utmost diligence in comforting the people, the hearts of the hundred millions have no division.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, twelve years have passed. Although the Central Plain has not been recovered and the enemy has not been exterminated, yet relying on the abundant virtue and grace of the ancestors and Your Majesty's utmost diligence in comforting the people, the hearts of the hundred millions remain undivided.

sentences.zh: 前年徽宗皇帝、寧德皇后崩問遽來，莫究不豫之狀，天下之人痛心疾首，而陛下方且屈意降志，以迎奉梓宮、請問諱日為事。

translations.literal: The year before last, news of the deaths of Emperor Huizong and Empress Ningde came suddenly; the circumstances of their illness were never investigated. All under Heaven were heartsick with grief, yet Your Majesty was just then humbling himself and lowering his resolve to receive the imperial coffin and inquire about the day of death.
translations.idiomatic: The year before last, news of the deaths of Emperor Huizong and Empress Ningde arrived suddenly; the circumstances of their illness were never investigated. All under Heaven were heartsick with grief, yet Your Majesty was just then humbling yourself and lowering your resolve to receive the imperial coffin and inquire about the day of death.

sentences.zh: 今又為此議，則人心日去，祖宗積累之業，陛下十二年勤撫之功，當決於此矣。

translations.literal: If this proposal is now adopted, the people's hearts will daily depart; the accumulated enterprise of the ancestors and the twelve years of Your Majesty's diligent comforting of the people will be decided at this moment.
translations.idiomatic: If this proposal is now adopted, the people's hearts will daily turn away; the accumulated enterprise of the ancestors and the twelve years of Your Majesty's diligent comforting of the people will be decided at this moment.

sentences.zh: 不識陛下亦嘗深謀而熟慮乎，抑在廷之臣不以告也？

translations.literal: I do not know whether Your Majesty has also deeply deliberated and carefully considered this, or whether the ministers at court have not informed you.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know whether Your Majesty has also deeply deliberated and carefully considered this, or whether the ministers at court have failed to inform you.

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「父母之仇不共戴天，兄弟之仇不反兵。」

translations.literal: The Rites says: "One does not live under the same Heaven with the murderer of one's parents; one does not turn back with weapons against the murderer of one's brother."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites says, "One does not live under the same Heaven with the murderer of one's parents; one does not turn back with weapons against the murderer of one's brother."

sentences.zh: 今陛下信仇敵之譎詐，而覬其肯和以紓目前之急，豈不失不共戴天、不反兵之義乎？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty trusts the deceit and treachery of the enemy and hopes they will agree to peace to relieve the present urgency—does this not violate the principle of not living under the same Heaven and not turning back with weapons?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty trusts the deceit and treachery of the enemy and hopes they will agree to peace to relieve the present urgency—does this not violate the principle of not living under the same Heaven and not turning back with weapons?

sentences.zh: 又況使人之來，以詔諭為名，以割地為要，今以不戴天之仇與之和，臣切為陛下痛惜之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the envoys have come in the name of imperial proclamation but with the demand of ceding territory; to make peace now with an enemy whom one cannot live under the same Heaven with—I deeply grieve and regret this for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the envoys have come in the name of imperial proclamation but with the demand of ceding territory; to make peace now with an enemy whom one cannot live under the same Heaven with—I deeply grieve and regret this for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 或以金國內亂，懼我襲己，故為甘言以緩王師。

translations.literal: Perhaps because the Jin state suffers internal disorder and fears we will attack them, they offer sweet words to slow the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps because the Jin state suffers internal disorder and fears we will attack them, they offer sweet words to slow the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 倘或果然，尤當鼓士卒之心，雪社稷之恥，尚何和之為務？

translations.literal: If this is indeed so, all the more should we rouse the hearts of the soldiers and wipe away the shame of the altars and ancestral temples—why should making peace be the task?
translations.idiomatic: If this is indeed so, all the more should we rouse the hearts of the soldiers and wipe away the shame of the altars and ancestral temples—why should making peace be the task?

sentences.zh: 又移書秦檜言：

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Qin Hui saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a letter to Qin Hui saying:

sentences.zh: 今北使在廷，天下憂憤，若和議一成，彼日益強，我日益怠，侵尋朘削，天下有被發左衽之憂。

translations.literal: Now the northern envoys are at court and all under Heaven are anxious and indignant; if a peace agreement is concluded, they will daily grow stronger while we daily grow slack, and through gradual erosion and diminution, all under Heaven will face the fear of having their hair cut and wearing barbarian dress.
translations.idiomatic: Now the northern envoys are at court and all under Heaven are anxious and indignant. If a peace agreement is concluded, they will daily grow stronger while we daily grow slack, and through gradual erosion and diminution, all under Heaven will face the fear of having their hair cut and wearing barbarian dress.

sentences.zh: 比者，竊聞主上以父兄未返，降志辱身於九重之中有年矣，然亦自是未聞金人悔過，還二帝於沙漠。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that the sovereign, because his father and elder brother have not returned, has for years humbled his will and debased himself within the Ninefold Enclosure; yet even so, I have never heard that the Jurchens have repented and returned the two emperors from the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have heard that the sovereign, because his father and elder brother have not returned, has for years humbled his will and debased himself within the Ninefold Enclosure; yet even so, I have never heard that the Jurchens have repented and returned the two emperors from the desert.

sentences.zh: 繼之梓宮崩問不詳，天下之人痛恨切骨，金人狼虎貪噬之性，不言可見。

translations.literal: Then came the unclear news of the imperial coffin's death; the people of all under Heaven hated this to the bone; the wolfish and tigerish, greedy and devouring nature of the Jurchens needs no words to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the unclear news of the imperial coffin's death; the people of all under Heaven hated this to the bone. The wolfish, tigerish, greedy, and devouring nature of the Jurchens needs no words to be seen.

sentences.zh: 天下方將以此望於相公，覬有以革其已然，豈意為之已。

translations.literal: All under Heaven was about to look to the Chancellor for this, hoping he would have the means to change what had already been done—who would have thought he would do it already.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven was about to look to the Chancellor for this, hoping he would have the means to change what had already been done—who would have thought he would do it already.

sentences.zh: 甚乎。

translations.literal: To such an extent.
translations.idiomatic: To such an extent.

sentences.zh: 今之上策，莫如自治。

translations.literal: The best policy now is none other than self-governance.
translations.idiomatic: The best policy now is none other than self-governance.

sentences.zh: 自治之要，內則進君子而遠小人，外則賞當功而罰當罪，使主上孝弟通於神明，道德成於安強，勿以小智孑義而圖大功，不勝幸甚。

translations.literal: The essentials of self-governance are: within, advance the noble and keep the petty at a distance; without, reward where merit warrants and punish where guilt warrants; cause the sovereign's filial piety and brotherliness to reach the spirits, and virtue and the Way to be established in peace and strength; do not use petty cleverness and narrow righteousness to pursue great achievement—I would be exceedingly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: The essentials of self-governance are: within, advance the noble and keep the petty at a distance; without, reward where merit warrants and punish where guilt warrants; cause the sovereign's filial piety and brotherliness to reach the spirits, and virtue and the Way to be established in peace and strength. Do not use petty cleverness and narrow righteousness to pursue great achievement—I would be exceedingly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 疏及書皆不報，於是焞固辭新命。

translations.literal: Neither the memorial nor the letter received any response; thereupon Tun firmly declined the new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Neither the memorial nor the letter received any response; thereupon Tun firmly declined the new appointment.

sentences.zh: 九年，以徽猷閣待制提舉萬壽觀兼侍講，又辭，且奏言：

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Glorious Learning, put in charge of Wanshou Abbey while also serving as lecturer, and again declined, submitting a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made attendant gentleman of the Hall of Glorious Learning, put in charge of Wanshou Abbey while also serving as lecturer, and again declined, submitting a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣職在勸講，蔑有發明，期月之間，病告相繼，坐竊厚祿，無補聖聰。

translations.literal: Your subject's duty is exhortation and lecturing, yet he has had nothing to expound; within a month illness leave followed in succession; he sits idly enjoying thick emoluments without benefiting the sage ear.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's duty is exhortation and lecturing, yet he has had nothing to expound. Within a month illness leave followed in succession; he sits idly enjoying thick emoluments without benefiting the sage ear.

sentences.zh: 先聖有言：「陳力就列，不能者止。」

translations.literal: The ancient sage said: "Offer your strength and take your place; if you cannot, then stop."
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sage said, "Offer your strength and take your place; if you cannot, then stop."

sentences.zh: 此當去者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason I should leave.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first reason I should leave.

sentences.zh: 臣起自草茅，誤膺召用，守道之語，形於訓詞，而臣貪戀寵榮，遂移素守，使朝廷非常不次之舉，獲懷利苟得之人。

translations.literal: Your subject rose from the grass and reeds and was mistakenly summoned to office; words of keeping to the Way appeared in the edict of appointment, yet your subject clung greedily to favor and glory and thus shifted his former steadfastness, causing the court's extraordinary and irregular promotion to obtain a man who harbors profit and seeks gain.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject rose from the grass and reeds and was mistakenly summoned to office. Words of keeping to the Way appeared in the edict of appointment, yet your subject clung greedily to favor and glory and thus shifted his former steadfastness, causing the court's extraordinary and irregular promotion to obtain a man who harbors profit and seeks gain.

sentences.zh: 此當去者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second reason I should leave.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason I should leave.

sentences.zh: 比嘗不量分守，言及國事，識見迂陋，已驗於今，跡其庸愚，豈堪時用。

translations.literal: Recently I overstepped my station and spoke of state affairs; my insight was narrow and crude and has already been proven by events; tracing my mediocrity and foolishness, how can I be fit for use in the age?
translations.idiomatic: Recently I overstepped my station and spoke of state affairs. My insight was narrow and crude and has already been proven by events; tracing my mediocrity and foolishness, how can I be fit for use in the age?

sentences.zh: 此當去者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third reason I should leave.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third reason I should leave.

sentences.zh: 臣自擢春官，未嘗供職，以疾乞去，更獲超遷，有何功勞，得以祗受。

translations.literal: Since your subject was promoted to the Ministry of Rites, he has never performed his duties; he requested leave on grounds of illness and yet received further extraordinary promotion—what merit does he have to receive this?
translations.idiomatic: Since your subject was promoted to the Ministry of Rites, he has never performed his duties. He requested leave on grounds of illness and yet received further extraordinary promotion—what merit does he have to receive this?

sentences.zh: 此當去者四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth reason I should leave.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth reason I should leave.

sentences.zh: 國朝典法，揆之禮經，年至七十，皆當致仕。

translations.literal: The statutes and laws of our dynasty, measured against the ritual classics, hold that at age seventy all should retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes and laws of our dynasty, measured against the ritual classics, hold that at age seventy all should retire from office.

sentences.zh: 今臣年齒已及，加以疾病，血氣既衰，戒之在得。

translations.literal: Now your subject's years have reached that mark, and illness is added besides; his vital force has already declined, and the warning against grasping applies.
translations.idiomatic: Now your subject's years have reached that mark, and illness is added besides. His vital force has already declined, and the warning against grasping applies.

sentences.zh: 此當去者五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth reason I should leave.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth reason I should leave.

sentences.zh: 臣聞聖君有從欲之仁，匹夫有莫奪之志，今臣有五當去之義，無一可留之理，乞檢會累奏，放歸田裡。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that a sage ruler has the benevolence to follow another's wish, and that a common man has a will that cannot be taken from him. Now your subject has five reasons he should leave and not one reason he may remain; he begs that his accumulated memorials be reviewed and that he be released to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that a sage ruler has the benevolence to follow another's wish, and that a common man has a will that cannot be taken from him. Now your subject has five reasons he should leave and not one reason he may remain; he begs that his accumulated memorials be reviewed and that he be released to return to his fields.

sentences.zh: 疏上，以焞提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Tun was made superintendent of Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Tun was made superintendent of Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 引年告老，轉一官致仕。

translations.literal: Citing his years he requested retirement; he was promoted one rank and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his years he requested retirement; he was promoted one rank and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 焞自入經筵，即乞休致，朝廷以禮留之；

translations.literal: From the time Tun entered the classics lecture, he requested retirement; the court retained him according to ritual;
translations.idiomatic: From the time Tun entered the classics lecture, he requested retirement; the court retained him according to ritual;

sentences.zh: 浚、鼎既去，秦檜當國，見焞議和疏及與檜書已不樂，至是，得求去之疏，遂不復留。

translations.literal: After Jun and Ding had left office, Qin Hui held the state; seeing Tun's memorial against peace and his letter to Hui, he was already displeased; when he received the memorial requesting leave, he no longer retained him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun and Ding had left office, Qin Hui held the state. Seeing Tun's memorial against peace and his letter to Hui, he was already displeased; when he received the memorial requesting leave, he no longer retained him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died.

sentences.zh: 當是時，學於程頤之門者固多君子，然求質直弘毅、實體力行若焞者蓋鮮。

translations.literal: At that time, those who studied at Cheng Yi's gate were indeed many noble men, yet to seek one upright, broad-minded, resolute, and earnest in practice like Tun was rare.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, those who studied at Cheng Yi's gate were indeed many noble men, yet to find one upright, broad-minded, resolute, and earnest in practice like Tun was rare.

sentences.zh: 頤嘗以「魯」許之，且曰：「我死，而不失其正者尹氏子也。」

translations.literal: Yi once approved him with the word "steadfast," and said: "When I die, the one who will not lose his rectitude is Master Yin's son."
translations.idiomatic: Yi once approved him with the word "steadfast," and said, "When I die, the one who will not lose his rectitude is Master Yin's son."

sentences.zh: 其言行見於《涪陵記善錄》為詳，有《論語解》及《門人問答》傳於世。

translations.literal: His words and conduct are recorded in detail in the Record of Good Deeds at Fuling; his Exposition of the Analects and Discussions with Disciples circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His words and conduct are recorded in detail in the Record of Good Deeds at Fuling; his Exposition of the Analects and Discussions with Disciples circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 楊時字中立，南劍將樂人。

translations.literal: Yang Shi, courtesy name Zhongli, was a man of Jiangle in Nanjian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi, styled Zhongli, was a native of Jiangle in Nanjian.

sentences.zh: 幼穎異，能屬文，稍長，潛心經史。

translations.literal: In youth he was precocious and unusual and could compose literary pieces; when somewhat older he devoted himself to the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was precocious and unusual and could compose literary pieces; when somewhat older he devoted himself to the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 熙寧九年，中進士第。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xining he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xining he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 時河南程顥與弟頤講孔、孟絕學於熙、豐之際，河、洛之士翕然師之。

translations.literal: At that time Cheng Hao of Henan and his younger brother Yi taught the lost learning of Confucius and Mencius during the Xining and Yuanfeng eras, and scholars of the Yellow and Luo rivers flocked to take them as teachers.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cheng Hao of Henan and his younger brother Yi taught the lost learning of Confucius and Mencius during the Xining and Yuanfeng eras, and scholars of the Yellow and Luo rivers flocked to take them as teachers.

sentences.zh: 時調官不赴，以師禮見顥於穎昌，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Shi did not go to his assigned post but, with the rites due a teacher, visited Hao at Yingchang; they got on extremely well.
translations.idiomatic: Shi did not go to his assigned post but, with the rites due a teacher, visited Hao at Yingchang; they got on extremely well.

sentences.zh: 其歸也，顥目送之曰：「吾道南矣。」

translations.literal: When he departed, Hao saw him off and said: "My Way goes south."
translations.idiomatic: When he departed, Hao saw him off and said, "My Way goes south."

sentences.zh: 四年而顥死，時聞之，設位哭寢門，而以書赴告同學者。

translations.literal: Four years later Hao died; when Shi heard of it, he set up a mourning seat at the bedroom door and sent letters to notify his fellow students.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later Hao died. When Shi heard of it, he set up a mourning seat at the bedroom door and sent letters to notify his fellow students.

sentences.zh: 至是，又見程頤於洛，時蓋年四十矣。

translations.literal: At this time he again visited Cheng Yi in Luoyang; Shi was then about forty years old.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he again visited Cheng Yi in Luoyang; Shi was then about forty years old.

sentences.zh: 一日見頤，頤偶瞑坐，時與游酢侍立不去，頤既覺，則門外雪深一尺矣。

translations.literal: One day when he visited Yi, Yi happened to be sitting with eyes closed in meditation; Shi and You Zuo stood attending and did not leave; when Yi awoke, the snow outside the gate was already a foot deep.
translations.idiomatic: One day when he visited Yi, Yi happened to be sitting with eyes closed in meditation. Shi and You Zuo stood attending and did not leave; when Yi awoke, the snow outside the gate was already a foot deep.

sentences.zh: 關西張載嘗著《西銘》，二程深推服之，時疑其近於兼愛，與其師頤辨論往復，聞理一分殊之說，始豁然無疑。

translations.literal: Zhang Zai of Guanxi once wrote the Western Inscription; the two Chengs deeply admired it. Shi doubted it was close to universal love and debated back and forth with his teacher Yi; when he heard the doctrine that principle is one but its manifestations are many, he suddenly became clear and had no further doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai of Guanxi once wrote the Western Inscription; the two Chengs deeply admired it. Shi doubted it was close to universal love and debated back and forth with his teacher Yi; when he heard the doctrine that principle is one but its manifestations are many, he suddenly became clear and had no further doubts.

sentences.zh: 杜門不仕者十年，久之，歷知瀏陽、餘杭、蕭山三縣，皆有惠政，民思之不忘。

translations.literal: He closed his door and did not take office for ten years; after a long time he successively served as magistrate of Liuyang, Yuhang, and Xiaoshan, and in each place had benevolent policies that the people remembered without forgetting.
translations.idiomatic: He closed his door and did not take office for ten years. After a long time he successively served as magistrate of Liuyang, Yuhang, and Xiaoshan, and in each place had benevolent policies that the people remembered without forgetting.

sentences.zh: 張舜民在諫垣，薦之，得荊州教授。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shunmin was in the remonstrance bureau, he recommended Shi, who obtained the post of professor in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shunmin was in the remonstrance bureau, he recommended Shi, who obtained the post of professor in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時安於州縣，未嘗求聞達，而德望日重，四方之士不遠千里從之遊，號曰龜山先生。

translations.literal: Shi was content in the prefectures and counties and never sought fame or advancement, yet his moral standing daily grew heavier; scholars from the four directions came from afar to study with him, and he was called Master Guishan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was content in the prefectures and counties and never sought fame or advancement, yet his moral standing daily grew heavier. Scholars from the four directions came from afar to study with him, and he was called Master Guishan.

sentences.zh: 時天下多故，有言於蔡京者，以為事至此必敗，宜引舊德老成置諸左右，庶幾猶可及，時宰是之。

translations.literal: At the time all under Heaven had many troubles; someone spoke to Cai Jing, saying that affairs had reached a point where defeat was inevitable and that old virtue and mature worth should be brought to the sovereign's side, so that perhaps it might still be in time; the chief minister agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all under Heaven had many troubles. Someone spoke to Cai Jing, saying that affairs had reached a point where defeat was inevitable and that old virtue and mature worth should be brought to the sovereign's side, so that perhaps it might still be in time; the chief minister agreed.

sentences.zh: 會有使高麗者，國主問龜山安在，使回以聞。

translations.literal: It happened that an envoy to Goryeo was sent; the Goryeo king asked where Master Guishan was, and when the envoy returned he reported this.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that an envoy to Goryeo was sent. The Goryeo king asked where Master Guishan was, and when the envoy returned he reported this.

sentences.zh: 召為秘書郎，遷著作郎。

translations.literal: Shi was summoned as Secretary and promoted to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was summoned as secretary and promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 及面對，奏曰：

translations.literal: When he faced the throne and addressed the court, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When he faced the throne and addressed the court, he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 堯、舜曰「允執厥中」，孟子曰「湯執中」，《洪範》曰「皇建其有極」，歷世聖人由斯道也。

translations.literal: Yao and Shun said "sincerely hold fast to the Mean," Mencius said "Tang held fast to the Mean," the Great Plan says "the sovereign establishes the supreme standard"—sage rulers through the ages followed this Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun said "sincerely hold fast to the Mean," Mencius said "Tang held fast to the Mean," the Great Plan says "the sovereign establishes the supreme standard"—sage rulers through the ages followed this Way.

sentences.zh: 熙寧之初，大臣文六藝之言以行其私，祖宗之法紛更殆盡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, great ministers clothed their private aims in the language of the Six Arts, and the laws of the ancestors were changed almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xining, great ministers clothed their private aims in the language of the Six Arts, and the laws of the ancestors were changed almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 元祐繼之，盡復祖宗之舊，熙寧之法一切廢革。

translations.literal: Yuanyou followed and fully restored the old ways of the ancestors, abolishing all the laws of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou followed and fully restored the old ways of the ancestors, abolishing all the laws of Xining.

sentences.zh: 至紹聖、崇寧抑又甚焉，凡元祐之政事著在令甲，皆焚之以滅其跡。

translations.literal: By Shaosheng and Chongning it was even worse; all Yuanyou policies recorded in active statutes were burned to erase their traces.
translations.idiomatic: By Shaosheng and Chongning it was even worse; all Yuanyou policies recorded in active statutes were burned to erase their traces.

sentences.zh: 自是分為二黨，縉紳之禍至今未殄。

translations.literal: From then on the court was divided into two factions, and the calamity of the gentry and officials has not yet been extinguished to this day.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the court was divided into two factions, and the calamity of the gentry and officials has not yet been extinguished to this day.

sentences.zh: 臣願明詔有司，條具祖宗之法，著為綱目，有宜於今者舉而行之，當損益者損益之，元祐、熙、豐姑置勿問，一趨於中而已。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that a clear edict be issued to the relevant offices to itemize the laws of the ancestors and set them forth as a program; what is suitable for the present should be implemented, what should be reduced or increased should be reduced or increased; Yuanyou and Xining and Yuanfeng should for the moment be set aside without inquiry, and all should tend toward the Mean alone.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes that a clear edict be issued to the relevant offices to itemize the laws of the ancestors and set them forth as a program. What is suitable for the present should be implemented; what should be reduced or increased should be reduced or increased. Yuanyou, Xining, and Yuanfeng should for the moment be set aside without inquiry, and all should tend toward the Mean alone.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方圖燕雲，虛內事外，時遂陳時政之弊，且謂：「燕雲之師宜退守內地，以省轉輸之勞，募邊民為弓弩手，以殺常勝軍之勢。」

translations.literal: The court was then planning for Yan and Yun, neglecting internal affairs for external ones; Shi thereupon set forth the defects of current policy and said: "The army for Yan and Yun should withdraw to guard the interior to save the labor of transport, and frontier people should be recruited as crossbowmen to check the momentum of the Ever-Victorious Army."
translations.idiomatic: The court was then planning for Yan and Yun, neglecting internal affairs for external ones. Shi thereupon set forth the defects of current policy and said, "The army for Yan and Yun should withdraw to guard the interior to save the labor of transport, and frontier people should be recruited as crossbowmen to check the momentum of the Ever-Victorious Army."

sentences.zh: 又言：「都城居四達之衢，無高山巨浸以為阻衛，士人懷異心，緩急不可倚仗。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The capital sits at a crossroads with no high mountains or great waters to serve as barriers; scholars harbor divergent hearts and cannot be relied upon in an emergency."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The capital sits at a crossroads with no high mountains or great waters to serve as barriers; scholars harbor divergent hearts and cannot be relied upon in an emergency."

sentences.zh: 執政不能用。

translations.literal: The chief ministers could not adopt this.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers could not adopt this.

sentences.zh: 登對，力陳君臣警戒，正在無虞之時，乞為《宣和會計錄》，以周知天下財物出入之數。

translations.literal: When he addressed the throne, he strenuously set forth the warning between ruler and minister that applies precisely in times free from worry, and requested compilation of an Xuanhe Accounting Record to give comprehensive knowledge of the income and expenditure of goods throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When he addressed the throne, he strenuously set forth the warning between ruler and minister that applies precisely in times free from worry, and requested compilation of an Xuanhe Accounting Record to give comprehensive knowledge of the income and expenditure of goods throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 徽宗首肯之。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 除邇英殿說書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Lecturer in the Hall of Eminent Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant lecturer in the Hall of Eminent Excellence.

sentences.zh: 聞金人入攻，謂執政曰：「今日事勢如積薪已然，當自奮勵，以竦動觀聽。

translations.literal: When he heard the Jurchens had entered in attack, he said to the chief ministers: "Today's situation is like piled kindling already set; we should rouse ourselves to stir and startle those who look on.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the Jurchens had entered in attack, he said to the chief ministers, "Today's situation is like piled kindling already set; we should rouse ourselves to stir and startle those who look on.

sentences.zh: 若示以怯懦之形，委靡不振，則事去矣。

translations.literal: If we show a timid and cowardly appearance and are listless and unresponsive, the affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If we show a timid and cowardly appearance and are listless and unresponsive, the affair is lost.

sentences.zh: 昔汲黯在朝，淮南寢謀。

translations.literal: In former times, when Ji An was at court, Huainan's plot went to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when Ji An was at court, Huainan's plot went to sleep.

sentences.zh: 論黯之才，未必能過公孫弘輩也，特其直氣可以鎮壓奸雄之心爾。

translations.literal: Judging An's talent, he was not necessarily superior to men like Gongsun Hong; it was only his upright spirit that could suppress the hearts of treacherous heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Judging An's talent, he was not necessarily superior to men like Gongsun Hong; it was only his upright spirit that could suppress the hearts of treacherous heroes.

sentences.zh: 朝廷威望弗振，使奸雄一以弘輩視之，則無復可為也。

translations.literal: If the court's prestige is not raised and treacherous heroes view it as they view men like Hong, then nothing more can be done.
translations.idiomatic: If the court's prestige is not raised and treacherous heroes view it as they view men like Hong, then nothing more can be done.

sentences.zh: 要害之地，當嚴為守備，比至都城，尚何及哉？

translations.literal: Key places should be strictly fortified for defense; by the time the enemy reaches the capital, what will be left to do?
translations.idiomatic: Key places should be strictly fortified for defense; by the time the enemy reaches the capital, what will be left to do?

sentences.zh: 近邊州軍宜堅壁清野，勿與之戰，使之自困。

translations.literal: Frontier prefectures and armies near the border should fortify their walls and clear the countryside, not giving battle, so that the enemy will exhaust themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier prefectures and armies near the border should fortify their walls and clear the countryside, not giving battle, so that the enemy will exhaust themselves.

sentences.zh: 若攻戰略地，當遣援兵追襲，使之腹背受敵，則可以制勝矣。」

translations.literal: If they attack and seize territory, relief troops should be sent to pursue and strike, causing them to be attacked front and rear; then victory can be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: If they attack and seize territory, relief troops should be sent to pursue and strike, causing them to be attacked front and rear; then victory can be achieved."

sentences.zh: 且謂：「今日之事，當以收人心為先。

translations.literal: He also said: "In today's affair, winning the people's hearts should come first.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In today's affair, winning the people's hearts should come first.

sentences.zh: 人心不附，雖有高城深池、堅甲利兵，不足恃也。

translations.literal: If the people's hearts are not attached, though there be high walls and deep moats, strong armor and sharp weapons, they are not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: If the people's hearts are not attached, though there be high walls and deep moats, strong armor and sharp weapons, they are not to be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 免夫之役，毒被海內，西城聚斂，東南花石，其害尤甚。

translations.literal: The corvée of exempted laborers poisons the whole realm; the western capital's exactions and the southeast's tribute stones are especially harmful.
translations.idiomatic: The corvée of exempted laborers poisons the whole realm; the western capital's exactions and the southeast's tribute stones are especially harmful.

sentences.zh: 前此蓋嘗罷之，詔墨未干，而花石供奉之舟已銜尾矣。

translations.literal: Previously these had been abolished, but before the edict ink was dry, the boats supplying tribute stones were already tailing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Previously these had been abolished, but before the edict ink was dry, the boats supplying tribute stones were already tailing one another.

sentences.zh: 今雖復申前令，而禍根不除，人誰信之？

translations.literal: Though the former order is now repeated, if the roots of the calamity are not removed, who will believe it?
translations.idiomatic: Though the former order is now repeated, if the roots of the calamity are not removed, who will believe it?

sentences.zh: 欲致人和，去此三者，正今日之先務也。」

translations.literal: To bring about harmony among the people, removing these three things is precisely today's foremost task."
translations.idiomatic: To bring about harmony among the people, removing these three things is precisely today's foremost task."

sentences.zh: 金人圍京城，勤王之兵四集，而莫相統一。

translations.literal: The Jurchens besieged the capital; armies coming to the sovereign's aid gathered from the four directions, yet none was unified in command.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens besieged the capital; armies coming to the sovereign's aid gathered from the four directions, yet none was unified in command.

sentences.zh: 時言：「唐九節度之師不立統帥，雖李、郭之善用兵，猶不免敗衄。

translations.literal: Shi said: "When Tang's nine frontier armies had no supreme commander, though Li and Guo were skilled in using troops, they still could not avoid defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "When Tang's nine frontier armies had no supreme commander, though Li and Guo were skilled in using troops, they still could not avoid defeat.

sentences.zh: 今諸路烏合之眾，臣謂當立統帥，一號令，示紀律，而後士卒始用命。」

translations.literal: Now the crowds assembled from various routes—I say a supreme commander should be established, one command and one order issued, discipline displayed, and only then will the soldiers begin to obey."
translations.idiomatic: Now the crowds assembled from various routes—I say a supreme commander should be established, one command and one order issued, discipline displayed, and only then will the soldiers begin to obey."

sentences.zh: 又言：「童貫為三路大帥，敵人侵疆，棄軍而歸，孥戮之有餘罪，朝廷置之不問，故梁方平、何灌皆相繼而遁。

translations.literal: He also said: "Tong Guan was grand marshal of the three routes; when the enemy invaded the frontier he abandoned the army and returned—a crime for which execution of his family would still leave a surplus; the court set this aside without inquiry, and so Liang Fangping and He Guan successively fled as well.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Tong Guan was grand marshal of the three routes. When the enemy invaded the frontier he abandoned the army and returned—a crime for which execution of his family would still leave a surplus. The court set this aside without inquiry, and so Liang Fangping and He Guan successively fled as well.

sentences.zh: 當正典刑，以為臣子不忠之戒。

translations.literal: The proper penalty of the law should be applied as a warning to disloyal ministers and sons.
translations.idiomatic: The proper penalty of the law should be applied as a warning to disloyal ministers and sons.

sentences.zh: 童貫握兵二十餘年，覆軍殺將，馴至今日，比聞防城仍用閹人，覆車之轍，不可復蹈。」

translations.literal: Tong Guan held military power for more than twenty years, destroyed armies and killed generals, and tamely reached the present day; I have lately heard that in defending the city eunuchs are still employed—the track of the overturned cart must not be trodden again."
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan held military power for more than twenty years, destroyed armies and killed generals, and tamely reached the present day. I have lately heard that in defending the city eunuchs are still employed—the track of the overturned cart must not be trodden again."

sentences.zh: 疏上，除右諫議大夫兼侍講。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he was appointed Right Remonstrance Official while also serving as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, he was appointed right remonstrance official while also serving as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 敵兵初退，議者欲割三鎮以講和，時極言其不可，曰：「河朔為朝廷重地，而三鎮又河朔之要藩也。

translations.literal: When the enemy troops first withdrew, some in council wished to cede the Three Prefectures to negotiate peace; Shi spoke forcefully against this, saying: "Hebei is a vital region for the court, and the Three Prefectures are the key bulwarks of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy troops first withdrew, some in council wished to cede the Three Prefectures to negotiate peace. Shi spoke forcefully against this, saying, "Hebei is a vital region for the court, and the Three Prefectures are the key bulwarks of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 自周世宗迄太祖、太宗，百戰而後得之，一旦棄之北庭，使敵騎疾驅，貫吾腹心，不數日可至京城。

translations.literal: From Emperor Shizong of Zhou down through Taizu and Taizong, they were obtained only after a hundred battles; to abandon them at once to the northern court would let enemy horsemen gallop swiftly and pierce our very heartland—in a few days they could reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Shizong of Zhou down through Taizu and Taizong, they were obtained only after a hundred battles. To abandon them at once to the northern court would let enemy horsemen gallop swiftly and pierce our very heartland—in a few days they could reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 今聞三鎮之民以死拒之，三鎮拒其前，吾以重兵躡其後，尚可為也。

translations.literal: Now I hear the people of the Three Prefectures are resisting to the death; with the Three Prefectures blocking them in front and our heavy troops pressing from behind, something can still be done.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear the people of the Three Prefectures are resisting to the death. With the Three Prefectures blocking them in front and our heavy troops pressing from behind, something can still be done.

sentences.zh: 若種師道、劉光世皆一時名將，始至而未用，乞召問方略。」

translations.literal: Men like Zhong Shidao and Liu Guangshi are famous generals of the age; they have just arrived and are not yet employed—I beg that they be summoned and questioned about strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zhong Shidao and Liu Guangshi are famous generals of the age. They have just arrived and are not yet employed—I beg that they be summoned and questioned about strategy."

sentences.zh: 疏上，欽宗詔出師，而議者多持兩端，時抗疏曰：「聞金人駐磁、相，破大名，劫虜驅掠，無有紀極，誓墨未干，而背不旋踵，吾雖欲專守和議，不可得也。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Qinzong ordered troops out, yet many in council held both ends; Shi submitted a forceful memorial saying: "I hear the Jurchens are stationed at Ci and Xiang, have broken Daming, and are plundering and driving captives without limit; the oath ink is not yet dry and they have already turned their backs without looking back—even if we wish to hold exclusively to peace talks, it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Qinzong ordered troops out, yet many in council held both ends. Shi submitted a forceful memorial saying, "I hear the Jurchens are stationed at Ci and Xiang, have broken Daming, and are plundering and driving captives without limit. The oath ink is not yet dry and they have already turned their backs without looking back—even if we wish to hold exclusively to peace talks, it cannot be obtained.

sentences.zh: 夫越數千里之遠，犯人國都，危道也。

translations.literal: To cross several thousand li and invade another state's capital is a perilous path.
translations.idiomatic: To cross several thousand li and invade another state's capital is a perilous path.

sentences.zh: 彼見勤王之師四面而集，亦懼而歸，非愛我而不攻。

translations.literal: When they see armies coming to the sovereign's aid gathering from the four directions, they too will fear and return—it is not that they love us and therefore do not attack.
translations.idiomatic: When they see armies coming to the sovereign's aid gathering from the four directions, they too will fear and return—it is not that they love us and therefore do not attack.

sentences.zh: 朝廷割三鎮二十州之地與之，是欲助寇而自攻也。

translations.literal: For the court to cede the land of the Three Prefectures and twenty prefectures to them is to wish to aid the bandits and attack ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: For the court to cede the land of the Three Prefectures and twenty prefectures to them is to wish to aid the bandits and attack ourselves.

sentences.zh: 聞肅王初與之約，及河而返，今挾之以往，此敗盟之大者。

translations.literal: I hear that when Prince Su first made an agreement with them, he returned when he reached the river; now they are taking him away with them—this is a great breach of the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that when Prince Su first made an agreement with them, he returned when he reached the river; now they are taking him away with them—this is a great breach of the agreement.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂朝廷宜以肅王為問，責其敗盟，必得肅王而後已。」

translations.literal: Your subject privately considers that the court should take Prince Su as the issue, charge them with breaching the agreement, and not stop until Prince Su is obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject privately considers that the court should take Prince Su as the issue, charge them with breaching the agreement, and not stop until Prince Su is obtained."

sentences.zh: 時太原圍閉數月，而姚古擁兵逗留不進，時上疏乞誅古以肅軍政，拔偏裨之可將者代之。

translations.literal: At the time Taiyuan had been besieged and closed for several months, yet Yao Gu held the army and lingered without advancing; Shi submitted a memorial requesting that Gu be executed to rectify military discipline and that a deputy commander fit to lead be chosen to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Taiyuan had been besieged and closed for several months, yet Yao Gu held the army and lingered without advancing. Shi submitted a memorial requesting that Gu be executed to rectify military discipline and that a deputy commander fit to lead be chosen to replace him.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: There was no response.

sentences.zh: 李綱之罷，太學生伏闕上書，乞留綱與種師道，軍民集者數十萬，朝廷欲防禁之。

translations.literal: When Li Gang was dismissed, Imperial Academy students prostrated themselves at the palace gate and submitted memorials requesting that Gang and Zhong Shidao be retained; soldiers and civilians who gathered numbered several hundred thousand, and the court wished to guard against and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang was dismissed, Imperial Academy students prostrated themselves at the palace gate and submitted memorials requesting that Gang and Zhong Shidao be retained. Soldiers and civilians who gathered numbered several hundred thousand, and the court wished to guard against and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 吳敏乞用時以靖太學，時得召對，言：「諸生伏闕紛紛，忠於朝廷，非有他意，但擇老成有行誼者，為之長貳，則將自定。」

translations.literal: Wu Min requested that Shi be used to pacify the Imperial Academy; Shi was summoned for an audience and said: "The students prostrating themselves at the gate are in an uproar out of loyalty to the court and have no other intent; only select mature men of conduct and righteousness to serve as their chief and deputy, and the commotion will settle of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Min requested that Shi be used to pacify the Imperial Academy. Shi was summoned for an audience and said, "The students prostrating themselves at the gate are in an uproar out of loyalty to the court and have no other intent. Only select mature men of conduct and righteousness to serve as their chief and deputy, and the commotion will settle of itself."

sentences.zh: 欽宗曰：「無逾於卿。」

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong said: "None surpasses you."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong said, "None surpasses you."

sentences.zh: 遂以時兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shi was additionally made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
