translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Shi was additionally made chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 首言：「三省政事所出，六曹分治，各有攸司。

translations.literal: He first said: "The Three Departments are where government affairs issue forth; the Six Ministries divide governance, each having its proper charge.
translations.idiomatic: He first said, "The Three Departments are where government affairs issue forth; the Six Ministries divide governance, each having its proper charge.

sentences.zh: 今乃別辟官屬，新進少年，未必賢於六曹長貳。」

translations.literal: Now separate offices are opened and newly advanced young men appointed—they are not necessarily more worthy than the chiefs and deputies of the Six Ministries."
translations.idiomatic: Now separate offices are opened and newly advanced young men appointed—they are not necessarily more worthy than the chiefs and deputies of the Six Ministries."

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 蔡京用事二十餘年，蠹國害民，幾危宗社，人所切齒，而論其罪者，莫知其所本也。

translations.literal: Cai Jing held power for more than twenty years, harming the state and injuring the people, nearly endangering the altars and ancestral temples; men gnash their teeth at him, yet those who discuss his crimes do not know their root.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing held power for more than twenty years, harming the state and injuring the people, nearly endangering the altars and ancestral temples. Men gnash their teeth at him, yet those who discuss his crimes do not know their root.

sentences.zh: 蓋京以繼述神宗為名，實挾王安石以圖身利，故推尊安石，加以王爵，配饗孔子廟庭。

translations.literal: Jing took continuing the work of Emperor Shenzong as his banner but in truth used Wang Anshi to pursue personal profit; therefore he exalted Anshi, granted him a princely title, and paired him in sacrifice at the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: Jing took continuing the work of Emperor Shenzong as his banner but in truth used Wang Anshi to pursue personal profit. Therefore he exalted Anshi, granted him a princely title, and paired him in sacrifice at the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 今日之禍，實安石有以啟之。

translations.literal: Today's calamity was in truth opened by Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Today's calamity was in truth opened by Anshi.

sentences.zh: 謹按安石挾管、商之術，飭六藝以文奸言，變亂祖宗法度。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that Anshi wielded the arts of Guan Zhong and Shang Yang, clothed treacherous words in the Six Arts, and changed and disrupted the laws and institutions of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consider that Anshi wielded the arts of Guan Zhong and Shang Yang, clothed treacherous words in the Six Arts, and changed and disrupted the laws and institutions of the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 當時司馬光已言其為害當見於數十年之後，今日之事，若合符契。

translations.literal: At the time Sima Guang already said its harm would appear several decades later; today's events fit the tally exactly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sima Guang already said its harm would appear several decades later; today's events fit the tally exactly.

sentences.zh: 其著為邪說以塗學者耳目，而敗壞其心術者，不可縷數，姑即一二事明之。

translations.literal: The heterodox doctrines he set forth to smear the eyes and ears of scholars and corrupt their minds and methods cannot be counted strand by strand; let one or two matters suffice to make this clear.
translations.idiomatic: The heterodox doctrines he set forth to smear the eyes and ears of scholars and corrupt their minds and methods cannot be counted strand by strand; let one or two matters suffice to make this clear.

sentences.zh: 昔神宗嘗稱美漢文惜百金以罷露台，安石乃言：「陛下若能以堯、舜之道治天下，雖竭天下以自奉不為過，守財之言非正理。」

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Shenzong once praised Emperor Wen of Han for sparing a hundred in gold to cancel the terrace platform; Anshi then said: "If Your Majesty can govern all under Heaven with the Way of Yao and Shun, though you exhaust all under Heaven to supply yourself it would not be excessive; words of guarding wealth are not correct principle."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Shenzong once praised Emperor Wen of Han for sparing a hundred in gold to cancel the terrace platform. Anshi then said, "If Your Majesty can govern all under Heaven with the Way of Yao and Shun, though you exhaust all under Heaven to supply yourself it would not be excessive; words of guarding wealth are not correct principle."

sentences.zh: 曾不知堯、舜茅茨土階。

translations.literal: He did not know that Yao and Shun had thatched roofs and earthen steps.
translations.idiomatic: He did not know that Yao and Shun had thatched roofs and earthen steps.

sentences.zh: 禹曰：「克儉於家」，則竭天下以自奉者，必非堯、舜之道。

translations.literal: Yu said, "Be sparing in your household"—therefore one who exhausts all under Heaven to supply himself cannot be following the Way of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Be sparing in your household"—therefore one who exhausts all under Heaven to supply himself cannot be following the Way of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 其後王黼以應奉花石之事，竭天下之力，號為享上，實安石有以倡之也。

translations.literal: Afterward Wang Fu, through the tribute-stone service, exhausted the strength of all under Heaven and called it serving the sovereign—in truth Anshi had advocated this.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Wang Fu, through the tribute-stone service, exhausted the strength of all under Heaven and called it serving the sovereign—in truth Anshi had advocated this.

sentences.zh: 其釋《鳧鷖》守成之詩，於末章則謂：「以道守成者，役使群眾，泰而不為驕，宰制萬物，費而不為侈，孰弊弊然以愛為事。」

translations.literal: In his interpretation of the "Wild Geese" ode on preserving the inheritance, in the final stanza he said: "One who preserves the inheritance by the Way employs the masses, is at ease without being arrogant, controls the myriad things, spends without being extravagant—who would toil and toil and take love as the task?"
translations.idiomatic: In his interpretation of the "Wild Geese" ode on preserving the inheritance, in the final stanza he said, "One who preserves the inheritance by the Way employs the masses, is at ease without being arrogant, controls the myriad things, spends without being extravagant—who would toil and toil and take love as the task?"

sentences.zh: 《詩》之所言，正謂能持盈則神祇祖考安樂之，而無後艱爾。

translations.literal: What the Odes speaks of is precisely that if one can hold fullness, then the spirits and ancestral fathers are at ease and there is no later hardship.
translations.idiomatic: What the Odes speaks of is precisely that if one can hold fullness, then the spirits and ancestral fathers are at ease and there is no later hardship.

sentences.zh: 自古釋之者，未有泰而不為驕、費而不為侈之說也。

translations.literal: From antiquity those who interpreted it never had the doctrine of being at ease without arrogance and spending without extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity those who interpreted it never had the doctrine of being at ease without arrogance and spending without extravagance.

sentences.zh: 安石獨倡為此說，以啟人主之侈心。

translations.literal: Anshi alone advocated this doctrine, thereby opening the sovereign's heart to extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi alone advocated this doctrine, thereby opening the sovereign's heart to extravagance.

sentences.zh: 後蔡京輩輕費妄用，以侈靡為事。

translations.literal: Later men like Cai Jing lightly spent and recklessly used funds, taking extravagance as their business.
translations.idiomatic: Later men like Cai Jing lightly spent and recklessly used funds, taking extravagance as their business.

sentences.zh: 安石邪說之害如此。

translations.literal: Such is the harm of Anshi's heterodox doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the harm of Anshi's heterodox doctrine.

sentences.zh: 伏望追奪王爵，明詔中外，毀去配享之像，使邪說淫辭不為學者之惑。

translations.literal: I respectfully hope his princely title may be posthumously revoked, that a clear edict be issued within and without, that the image paired in sacrifice be destroyed, and that heterodox doctrines and licentious words no longer confuse scholars.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully hope his princely title may be posthumously revoked, that a clear edict be issued within and without, that the image paired in sacrifice be destroyed, and that heterodox doctrines and licentious words no longer confuse scholars.

sentences.zh: 疏上，安石遂降從祀之列。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Anshi was reduced to the secondary rank of those sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Anshi was reduced to the secondary rank of those sacrificed to.

sentences.zh: 士之習王氏學取科第者，已數十年，不復知其非，忽聞以為邪說，議論紛然。

translations.literal: Scholars who had studied Wang's learning to obtain examination degrees had already done so for several decades and no longer knew it was wrong; suddenly hearing it called heterodox doctrine, debate was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who had studied Wang's learning to obtain examination degrees had already done so for several decades and no longer knew it was wrong. Suddenly hearing it called heterodox doctrine, debate was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 諫官馮澥力主王氏，上疏詆時。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Feng Xi forcefully upheld the Wang school and submitted a memorial slandering Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Feng Xi forcefully upheld the Wang school and submitted a memorial slandering Shi.

sentences.zh: 會學官中有紛爭者，有旨學官並罷，時亦罷祭酒。

translations.literal: It happened that there was contention among the academy officials; an edict dismissed all academy officials, and Shi was also dismissed as Chancellor of Education.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that there was contention among the academy officials. An edict dismissed all academy officials, and Shi was also dismissed as chancellor of education.

sentences.zh: 時又言：「元祐黨籍中，惟司馬光一人獨褒顯，而未及呂公著、韓維、范純仁、呂大防、安燾輩。

translations.literal: Shi also said: "Among the Yuanyou faction register, only Sima Guang alone has been singled out for praise, while Lü Gongzhu, Han Wei, Fan Chunren, Lü Dafang, An Tao, and others have not yet been included.
translations.idiomatic: Shi also said, "Among the Yuanyou faction register, only Sima Guang alone has been singled out for praise, while Lü Gongzhu, Han Wei, Fan Chunren, Lü Dafang, An Tao, and others have not yet been included.

sentences.zh: 建中初言官陳瓘已褒贈，而未及鄒浩。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, remonstrance official Chen Guan had already been posthumously honored, but Zou Hao had not yet been included."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong, remonstrance official Chen Guan had already been posthumously honored, but Zou Hao had not yet been included."

sentences.zh: 於是元祐諸臣皆次第牽復。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officials of the Yuanyou faction were all successively restored.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the officials of the Yuanyou faction were all successively restored.

sentences.zh: 尋四上章乞罷諫省，除給事中，辭，乞致仕，除徽猷閣直學士、提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted four memorials requesting dismissal from the remonstrance bureau; he was appointed Drafting Attendant, declined, requested retirement, and was made Direct Attendant of the Hall of Glorious Learning and put in charge of Chongfu Abbey on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he submitted four memorials requesting dismissal from the remonstrance bureau. He was appointed drafting attendant, declined, requested retirement, and was made direct attendant of the Hall of Glorious Learning and put in charge of Chongfu Abbey on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 時力辭直學士之命，改除徽猷閣待制、提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: Shi strenuously declined the direct attendant appointment and was instead made Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Glorious Learning and put in charge of Chongfu Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Shi strenuously declined the direct attendant appointment and was instead made attendant gentleman of the Hall of Glorious Learning and put in charge of Chongfu Abbey.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，猶上書乞選將練兵，為戰守之備。

translations.literal: When he took leave of the throne, he still submitted a memorial requesting selection of generals and training of troops as preparation for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave of the throne, he still submitted a memorial requesting selection of generals and training of troops as preparation for war and defense.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，除工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, Shi was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne, Shi was appointed vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 陛對言：「自古聖賢之君，未有不以典學為務。」

translations.literal: When he addressed the throne he said: "From antiquity sage and worthy rulers have none who did not make canonical learning their task."
translations.idiomatic: When he addressed the throne he said, "From antiquity sage and worthy rulers have none who did not make canonical learning their task."

sentences.zh: 除兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed reader.

sentences.zh: 乞修《建炎會計錄》，乞恤勤王之兵，乞寬假言者。

translations.literal: He requested compilation of the Jianyan Accounting Record, relief for armies coming to the sovereign's aid, and leniency for those who spoke out.
translations.idiomatic: He requested compilation of the Jianyan Accounting Record, relief for armies coming to the sovereign's aid, and leniency for those who spoke out.

sentences.zh: 連章丐外，以龍圖閣直學士提舉杭州洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He submitted successive memorials requesting outside appointment and was made Direct Attendant of the Hall of Dragon Pictures and put in charge of Dongxiao Abbey in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted successive memorials requesting outside appointment and was made direct attendant of the Hall of Dragon Pictures and put in charge of Dongxiao Abbey in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 已而告老，以本官致仕，優遊林泉，以著書講學為事。

translations.literal: Before long he reported old age and retired from office at his present rank, leisurely roaming forests and springs and taking writing books and lecturing as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he reported old age and retired from office at his present rank, leisurely roaming forests and springs and taking writing books and lecturing as his occupation.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十三，謚文靖。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-three and was posthumously titled Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age eighty-three and was posthumously titled Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 時在東郡，所交皆天下士，先達陳瓘、鄒浩皆以師禮事時。

translations.literal: When Shi was in the eastern commandery, those he associated with were all eminent men under Heaven; senior figures Chen Guan and Zou Hao both treated Shi with the rites due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi was in the eastern commandery, those he associated with were all eminent men under Heaven. Senior figures Chen Guan and Zou Hao both treated Shi with the rites due a teacher.

sentences.zh: 暨渡江，東南學者推時為程氏正宗。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi, scholars of the southeast regarded Shi as the orthodox lineage of the Cheng school.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangzi, scholars of the southeast regarded Shi as the orthodox lineage of the Cheng school.

sentences.zh: 與胡安國往來講論尤多。

translations.literal: He exchanged visits and discussions with Hu Anguo more than with anyone else.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged visits and discussions with Hu Anguo more than with anyone else.

sentences.zh: 時浮沉州縣四十有七年，晚居諫省，僅九十日，凡所論列皆切於世道，而其大者，則辟王氏經學，排靖康和議，使邪說不作。

translations.literal: Shi drifted through prefectures and counties for forty-seven years; late in life he dwelt in the remonstrance bureau for only ninety days; all he set forth was pertinent to the age's Way, and among the great matters he rebutted Wang's classical learning and rejected the Jingkang peace agreement, causing heterodox doctrines not to arise.
translations.idiomatic: Shi drifted through prefectures and counties for forty-seven years. Late in life he dwelt in the remonstrance bureau for only ninety days. All he set forth was pertinent to the age's Way, and among the great matters he rebutted Wang's classical learning and rejected the Jingkang peace agreement, causing heterodox doctrines not to arise.

sentences.zh: 凡紹興初崇尚元祐學術，而朱熹、張栻之學得程氏之正，其源委脈絡皆出於時。

translations.literal: Generally, the early Shaoxing esteem for Yuanyou learning, and the learning of Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi obtaining the correct transmission of the Cheng school—all their sources, branches, and connecting threads issued from Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, the early Shaoxing esteem for Yuanyou learning, and the learning of Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi obtaining the correct transmission of the Cheng school—all their sources, branches, and connecting threads issued from Shi.

sentences.zh: 子迪，力學通經，亦嘗師程頤雲。

translations.literal: His son Di studied hard and mastered the classics; he also once studied under Cheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Di studied hard and mastered the classics; he also once studied under Cheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 羅從彥

translations.literal: Luo Congyan
translations.idiomatic: Luo Congyan

sentences.zh: 羅從彥字仲素，南劍人。

translations.literal: Luo Congyan, courtesy name Zhongsu, was a man of Nanjian.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Congyan, styled Zhongsu, was a native of Nanjian.

sentences.zh: 以累舉恩為惠州博羅縣主簿。

translations.literal: Through repeated examination privileges he was appointed Chief Clerk of Boluo County in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated examination privileges he was appointed chief clerk of Boluo County in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 聞同郡楊時得河南程氏學，慨然慕之，及時為蕭山令，遂徒步往學焉。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yang Shi of the same commandery had obtained the learning of the Cheng school of Henan, he admired this and set out; when Shi was magistrate of Xiaoshan, he went on foot to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Yang Shi of the same commandery had obtained the learning of the Cheng school of Henan, he admired this and set out. When Shi was magistrate of Xiaoshan, he went on foot to study under him.

sentences.zh: 時熟察之，乃喜曰：「惟從彥可與言道。」

translations.literal: Shi closely observed him and then said with pleasure: "Only Congyan can be spoken to about the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Shi closely observed him and then said with pleasure, "Only Congyan can be spoken to about the Way."

sentences.zh: 於是日益以親，時弟子千餘人，無及從彥者。

translations.literal: Thereafter they daily grew closer; among Shi's more than a thousand disciples, none matched Congyan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they daily grew closer; among Shi's more than a thousand disciples, none matched Congyan.

sentences.zh: 從彥初見時三日，即驚汗浹背，曰：「不至是，幾虛過一生矣。」

translations.literal: When Congyan first met Shi for three days, he broke out in startled sweat soaking his back and said: "Had it not come to this, I would nearly have wasted my whole life."
translations.idiomatic: When Congyan first met Shi for three days, he broke out in startled sweat soaking his back and said, "Had it not come to this, I would nearly have wasted my whole life."

sentences.zh: 嘗與時講《易》，至《乾》九四爻，云：「伊川說甚善。」

translations.literal: Once when he and Shi were discussing the Changes, reaching the fourth line of the Qian hexagram, he said: "Master Yichuan's explanation is very good."
translations.idiomatic: Once when he and Shi were discussing the Changes, reaching the fourth line of the Qian hexagram, he said, "Master Yichuan's explanation is very good."

sentences.zh: 從彥即鬻田走洛，見頤問之，頤反覆以告，從彥謝曰：「聞之龜山具是矣。」

translations.literal: Congyan immediately sold his fields and went to Luoyang, saw Yi and questioned him; Yi explained back and forth and told him; Congyan thanked him and said: "What I heard from Master Guishan is entirely correct."
translations.idiomatic: Congyan immediately sold his fields and went to Luoyang, saw Yi and questioned him. Yi explained back and forth and told him; Congyan thanked him and said, "What I heard from Master Guishan is entirely correct."

sentences.zh: 乃歸卒業。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned and completed his training.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he returned and completed his training.

sentences.zh: 沙縣陳淵，楊時之婿也，嘗詣從彥，必竟日乃返，謂人曰：「自吾交仲素，日聞所不聞，奧學清節，真南州之冠冕也。

translations.literal: Chen Yuan of Shaxian, who was Yang Shi's son-in-law, once visited Congyan and always stayed a whole day before returning; he told others: "Since I befriended Zhongsu, each day I hear what I had not heard before; his profound learning and pure integrity are truly the crown of the southern realm.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuan of Shaxian, who was Yang Shi's son-in-law, once visited Congyan and always stayed a whole day before returning. He told others, "Since I befriended Zhongsu, each day I hear what I had not heard before; his profound learning and pure integrity are truly the crown of the southern realm.

sentences.zh: 既而築室山中，絕意仕進，終日端坐，間謁時將溪上，吟詠而歸，恆充然自得焉。

translations.literal: Before long he built a dwelling in the mountains and utterly abandoned thoughts of entering office; all day he sat upright; occasionally visiting Shi along the stream, he would chant poetry on the return, always filled with contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he built a dwelling in the mountains and utterly abandoned thoughts of entering office. All day he sat upright; occasionally visiting Shi along the stream, he would chant poetry on the return, always filled with contentment.

sentences.zh: 嘗采祖宗故事為《遵堯錄》，靖康中，擬獻闕下，會國難不果。

translations.literal: He once collected stories of the ancestors' precedents into the Record of Following Yao; during the Jingkang era he planned to present it at court, but because of national calamity this did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: He once collected stories of the ancestors' precedents into the Record of Following Yao. During the Jingkang era he planned to present it at court, but because of national calamity this did not come to pass.

sentences.zh: 嘗與學者論治曰：「祖宗法度不可廢，德澤不可恃。

translations.literal: He once discussed governance with scholars, saying: "The laws and institutions of the ancestors cannot be abolished; virtue and grace cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: He once discussed governance with scholars, saying, "The laws and institutions of the ancestors cannot be abolished; virtue and grace cannot be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 廢法度則變亂之事起，恃德澤則驕佚之心生。

translations.literal: Abolish laws and institutions and disorder will arise; rely on virtue and grace and hearts of arrogance and dissipation will be born.
translations.idiomatic: Abolish laws and institutions and disorder will arise; rely on virtue and grace and hearts of arrogance and dissipation will be born.

sentences.zh: 自古德澤最厚莫若堯、舜，向使子孫可恃，則堯、舜必傳其子。

translations.literal: From antiquity none had thicker virtue and grace than Yao and Shun; if their descendants could be relied upon, then Yao and Shun would certainly have transmitted to their sons.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity none had thicker virtue and grace than Yao and Shun; if their descendants could be relied upon, then Yao and Shun would certainly have transmitted to their sons.

sentences.zh: 法度之明莫如周，向使子孫世守文、武、成、康之遺緒，雖至今存可也。」

translations.literal: None had clearer laws and institutions than Zhou; if their descendants had generation after generation preserved the legacy of Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang, they could have endured even to the present."
translations.idiomatic: None had clearer laws and institutions than Zhou; if their descendants had generation after generation preserved the legacy of Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang, they could have endured even to the present."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「君子在朝則天下必治，蓋君子進則常有亂世之言，使人主多憂而善心生，故治。

translations.literal: He also said: "When noble men are at court, all under Heaven is necessarily well governed, for when noble men advance they constantly speak words of a chaotic age, causing the sovereign much worry and good hearts to be born—therefore there is order.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When noble men are at court, all under Heaven is necessarily well governed, for when noble men advance they constantly speak words of a chaotic age, causing the sovereign much worry and good hearts to be born—therefore there is order.

sentences.zh: 小人在朝則天下亂，蓋小人進則常有治世之言，使人主多樂而怠心生，故亂。」

translations.literal: When petty men are at court, all under Heaven is chaotic, for when petty men advance they constantly speak words of an ordered age, causing the sovereign much pleasure and hearts of slackness to be born—therefore there is chaos."
translations.idiomatic: When petty men are at court, all under Heaven is chaotic, for when petty men advance they constantly speak words of an ordered age, causing the sovereign much pleasure and hearts of slackness to be born—therefore there is chaos."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「天下之變不起於四方，而起於朝廷。

translations.literal: He also said: "Transformations in all under Heaven do not arise from the four directions but arise from the court.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Transformations in all under Heaven do not arise from the four directions but arise from the court.

sentences.zh: 譬如人之傷氣，則寒暑易侵；

translations.literal: It is like when a person's vital energy is injured, then cold and heat easily invade;
translations.idiomatic: It is like when a person's vital energy is injured, then cold and heat easily invade;

sentences.zh: 木之傷心，則風雨易折。

translations.literal: when a tree's heart is injured, then wind and rain easily break it.
translations.idiomatic: when a tree's heart is injured, then wind and rain easily break it.

sentences.zh: 故內有林甫之奸，則外必有祿山之亂，內有盧杞之奸，則外必有朱泚之叛。」

translations.literal: Therefore when within there is the treachery of a Li Linfu, without there is necessarily the rebellion of an An Lushan; when within there is the treachery of a Lu Qi, without there is necessarily the revolt of a Zhu Ci."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when within there is the treachery of a Li Linfu, without there is necessarily the rebellion of an An Lushan; when within there is the treachery of a Lu Qi, without there is necessarily the revolt of a Zhu Ci."

sentences.zh: 其論士行曰：「周、孔之心使人明道，學者果能明道，則周、孔之心，深自得之。

translations.literal: In his discussion of scholars' conduct he said: "The hearts of Zhou and Confucius make men clarify the Way; if scholars can truly clarify the Way, then the hearts of Zhou and Confucius they will deeply obtain for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In his discussion of scholars' conduct he said, "The hearts of Zhou and Confucius make men clarify the Way; if scholars can truly clarify the Way, then the hearts of Zhou and Confucius they will deeply obtain for themselves.

sentences.zh: 三代人才得周、孔之心，而明道者多，故視死生去就如寒暑晝夜之移，而忠義行之者易。

translations.literal: Talents of the Three Dynasties obtained the hearts of Zhou and Confucius, and those who clarified the Way were many; therefore they viewed life and death, departure and staying as the shift of cold, heat, day, and night, and loyalty and righteousness were easy to practice.
translations.idiomatic: Talents of the Three Dynasties obtained the hearts of Zhou and Confucius, and those who clarified the Way were many. Therefore they viewed life and death, departure and staying as the shift of cold, heat, day, and night, and loyalty and righteousness were easy to practice.

sentences.zh: 至漢、唐以經術古文相尚，而失周、孔之心，故經術自董生、公孫弘倡之，古文自韓愈、柳宗元啟之，於是明道者寡，故視死生去就如萬鈞九鼎之重，而忠義行之者難。

translations.literal: By Han and Tang, classical learning and ancient prose were mutually esteemed, yet the hearts of Zhou and Confucius were lost; therefore from the time classical learning was advocated by Dong Zhongshu and Gongsun Hong and ancient prose was opened by Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan, those who clarified the Way were few; therefore they viewed life and death, departure and staying as the weight of ten thousand jun and the nine tripods, and loyalty and righteousness were hard to practice.
translations.idiomatic: By Han and Tang, classical learning and ancient prose were mutually esteemed, yet the hearts of Zhou and Confucius were lost. Therefore from the time classical learning was advocated by Dong Zhongshu and Gongsun Hong and ancient prose was opened by Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan, those who clarified the Way were few. Therefore they viewed life and death, departure and staying as the weight of ten thousand jun and the nine tripods, and loyalty and righteousness were hard to practice.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，學者所見，自漢、唐喪矣。」

translations.literal: Alas, what scholars have seen has been lost since Han and Tang."
translations.idiomatic: Alas, what scholars have seen has been lost since Han and Tang."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「士之立朝，要以正直忠厚為本。

translations.literal: He also said: "When scholars stand at court, they should take uprightness and deep loyalty as their root.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When scholars stand at court, they should take uprightness and deep loyalty as their root.

sentences.zh: 正直則朝廷無過失，忠厚則天下無嗟怨。

translations.literal: Uprightness then the court has no faults; deep loyalty then all under Heaven has no sighs of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Uprightness then the court has no faults; deep loyalty then all under Heaven has no sighs of resentment.

sentences.zh: 一於正直而不忠厚，則漸入於刻。

translations.literal: If one is solely upright without deep loyalty, one gradually enters harshness.
translations.idiomatic: If one is solely upright without deep loyalty, one gradually enters harshness.

sentences.zh: 一於忠厚而不正直，則流入於懦。」

translations.literal: If one is solely deep loyal without uprightness, one flows into cowardice."
translations.idiomatic: If one is solely deep loyal without uprightness, one flows into cowardice."

sentences.zh: 其議論醇正類此。

translations.literal: His discussions were pure and correct like this.
translations.idiomatic: His discussions were pure and correct like this.

sentences.zh: 朱熹謂：「龜山倡道東南，士之遊其門者甚眾，然潛思力行、任重詣極如仲素，一人而已。」

translations.literal: Zhu Xi said: "Master Guishan advocated the Way in the southeast; scholars who visited his gate were very many, yet in silent reflection and earnest practice, bearing heavy responsibility and reaching the utmost, like Zhongsu, there was only one man."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi said, "Master Guishan advocated the Way in the southeast; scholars who visited his gate were very many, yet in silent reflection and earnest practice, bearing heavy responsibility and reaching the utmost, like Zhongsu, there was only one man."

sentences.zh: 紹興中卒，學者稱之曰豫章先生，淳祐間謚文質。

translations.literal: He died in the Shaoxing era; scholars called him Master Yuzhang; in the Chunyou era he was posthumously titled Wenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Shaoxing era; scholars called him Master Yuzhang; in the Chunyou era he was posthumously titled Wenzhi.

sentences.zh: 李侗字願中，南劍州劍浦人。

translations.literal: Li Tong, courtesy name Yuanzhong, was a man of Jianpu in Nanjian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong, styled Yuanzhong, was a native of Jianpu in Nanjian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年二十四，聞郡人羅從彥得河、洛之學，遂以書謁之，其略曰：

translations.literal: At age twenty-four, hearing that Luo Congyan of his commandery had obtained the learning of the Yellow and Luo rivers, he sent a letter calling on him; the gist was:
translations.idiomatic: At age twenty-four, hearing that Luo Congyan of his commandery had obtained the learning of the Yellow and Luo rivers, he sent a letter calling on him. The gist was:

sentences.zh: 侗聞之，天下有三本焉，父生之，師教之，君治之，闕其一則本不立。

translations.literal: Tong has heard that all under Heaven has three roots: the father begets one, the teacher instructs one, the ruler governs one—if one is lacking the root cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: Tong has heard that all under Heaven has three roots: the father begets one, the teacher instructs one, the ruler governs one—if one is lacking the root cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 古之聖賢莫不有師，其肄業之勤惰，涉道之淺深，求益之先後，若存若亡，其詳不可得而考。

translations.literal: Ancient sages and worthies all had teachers; the diligence or slackness of their study, the shallowness or depth of their entry into the Way, the priority or delay of seeking increase—as if present, as if absent—the details cannot be examined.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sages and worthies all had teachers. The diligence or slackness of their study, the shallowness or depth of their entry into the Way, the priority or delay of seeking increase—as if present, as if absent—the details cannot be examined.

sentences.zh: 惟洙、泗之間，七十二弟子之徒，議論問答，具在方冊，有足稽焉，是得夫子而益明矣。

translations.literal: Only between Zhu and Si, the disciples of the seventy-two, their discussions, questions, and answers are fully preserved in records and can be traced; this was obtaining the Master and thereby becoming clearer.
translations.idiomatic: Only between Zhu and Si, the disciples of the seventy-two, their discussions, questions, and answers are fully preserved in records and can be traced; this was obtaining the Master and thereby becoming clearer.

sentences.zh: 孟氏之後，道失其傳，枝分派別，自立門戶，天下真儒不復見於世。

translations.literal: After Mencius, the Way lost its transmission; branches split and schools established their own gates; true Confucians of all under Heaven no longer appeared in the world.
translations.idiomatic: After Mencius, the Way lost its transmission; branches split and schools established their own gates; true Confucians of all under Heaven no longer appeared in the world.

sentences.zh: 其聚徒成群，所以相傳授者，句讀文義而已爾，謂之熄焉可也。

translations.literal: Those who gathered disciples and formed groups to transmit instruction did nothing but phrase-reading and textual meaning—that can be called extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who gathered disciples and formed groups to transmit instruction did nothing but phrase-reading and textual meaning—that can be called extinguished.

sentences.zh: 其惟先生服膺龜山先生之講席有年矣，況嘗及伊川先生之門，得不傳之道於千五百年之後，性明而修，行完而潔，擴之以廣大，體之以仁恕，精深微妙，各極其至，漢、唐諸儒無近似者。

translations.literal: Only the Master has attended Master Guishan's lecture seat for years; moreover he once reached the gate of Master Yichuan, and thus obtained the transmitted Way after fifteen hundred years—nature clear and cultivated, conduct complete and pure, expanded with breadth and largeness, embodied with benevolence and forgiveness, profound, refined, subtle, and wondrous, each reaching its utmost; Han and Tang Confucians had none approximating him.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Master has attended Master Guishan's lecture seat for years. Moreover he once reached the gate of Master Yichuan, and thus obtained the transmitted Way after fifteen hundred years—nature clear and cultivated, conduct complete and pure, expanded with breadth and largeness, embodied with benevolence and forgiveness, profound, refined, subtle, and wondrous, each reaching its utmost. Han and Tang Confucians had none approximating him.

sentences.zh: 至於不言而飲人以和，與人並立而使人化，如春風發物，蓋亦莫知其所以然也。

translations.literal: As for not speaking yet giving men harmony to drink, standing with men yet causing them to be transformed—it is like the spring wind sending forth things; one also does not know how this comes to be so.
translations.idiomatic: As for not speaking yet giving men harmony to drink, standing with men yet causing them to be transformed—it is like the spring wind sending forth things; one also does not know how this comes to be so.

sentences.zh: 凡讀聖賢之書，粗有識見者，孰不願得授經門下，以質所疑，至於異論之人，固當置而勿論也。

translations.literal: All who read the books of sages and worthies and have some measure of insight—who does not wish to receive instruction at your gate and submit what they doubt? As for men of divergent doctrines, they should indeed be set aside and not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: All who read the books of sages and worthies and have some measure of insight—who does not wish to receive instruction at your gate and submit what they doubt? As for men of divergent doctrines, they should indeed be set aside and not discussed.

sentences.zh: 侗之愚鄙，徒以習舉子業，不得服役於門下，而今日拳拳欲求教者，以謂所求有大於利祿也。

translations.literal: Tong's foolishness and baseness—he merely because of studying examination essays could not serve at your gate; yet today, earnestly and sincerely, he wishes to seek instruction because he considers what he seeks greater than profit and emolument.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's foolishness and baseness—he merely because of studying examination essays could not serve at your gate. Yet today, earnestly and sincerely, he wishes to seek instruction because he considers what he seeks greater than profit and emolument.

sentences.zh: 抑侗聞之，道可以治心，猶食之充飽，衣之御寒也。

translations.literal: Moreover Tong has heard that the Way can govern the heart, just as food fills hunger and clothing wards off cold.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Tong has heard that the Way can govern the heart, just as food fills hunger and clothing wards off cold.

sentences.zh: 人有迫於饑寒之患者，皇皇焉為衣食之謀，造次顛沛，未始忘也。

translations.literal: When people are pressed by the suffering of hunger and cold, they are frantic in schemes for food and clothing; in haste and distress they never forget.
translations.idiomatic: When people are pressed by the suffering of hunger and cold, they are frantic in schemes for food and clothing; in haste and distress they never forget.

sentences.zh: 至於心之不治，有沒世不知慮，豈愛心不若口體哉，弗思甚矣。

translations.literal: As for the heart not being governed, some go their whole lives without considering it—can love for the heart be less than for mouth and body? How greatly they fail to think.
translations.idiomatic: As for the heart not being governed, some go their whole lives without considering it—can love for the heart be less than for mouth and body? How greatly they fail to think.

sentences.zh: 侗不量資質之陋，徒以祖父以儒學起家，不忍墜箕裘之業，孜孜矻矻為利祿之學，雖知真儒有作，聞風而起，固不若先生親炙之得於動靜語默之間，目擊而意全也。

translations.literal: Tong does not measure the baseness of his endowment; he merely because his grandfather and father established the family through Confucian learning cannot bear to let the inherited mantle fall; diligently and tirelessly he pursues learning for profit and emolument; though he knows true Confucians have arisen and he rises at the report of their wind, it is certainly not like obtaining it from the Master through personal instruction between movement and stillness, speech and silence, seeing with the eyes and the meaning fully grasped.
translations.idiomatic: Tong does not measure the baseness of his endowment. He merely because his grandfather and father established the family through Confucian learning cannot bear to let the inherited mantle fall. Diligently and tirelessly he pursues learning for profit and emolument; though he knows true Confucians have arisen and he rises at the report of their wind, it is certainly not like obtaining it from the Master through personal instruction between movement and stillness, speech and silence, seeing with the eyes and the meaning fully grasped.

sentences.zh: 今生二十有四歲，茫乎未有所止，燭理未明而是非無以辨，宅心不廣而喜怒易以搖，操履不完而悔吝多，精神不充而智巧襲，揀焉而不淨，守焉而不敷，朝夕恐懼，不啻如饑寒切身者求充飢御寒之具也。

translations.literal: Now at age twenty-four, aimlessly he has not yet stopped anywhere; principles are not clear and right and wrong cannot be distinguished; the heart's dwelling is not broad and joy and anger are easily shaken; conduct is incomplete and regret and shame are many; spirit is not full and cleverness and artifice encroach; he selects but is not pure, guards but does not spread; morning and evening he fears, no less than when hunger and cold press upon the body he seeks means to fill hunger and ward off cold.
translations.idiomatic: Now at age twenty-four, aimlessly he has not yet stopped anywhere. Principles are not clear and right and wrong cannot be distinguished; the heart's dwelling is not broad and joy and anger are easily shaken; conduct is incomplete and regret and shame are many; spirit is not full and cleverness and artifice encroach. He selects but is not pure, guards but does not spread; morning and evening he fears, no less than when hunger and cold press upon the body he seeks means to fill hunger and ward off cold.

sentences.zh: 不然，安敢以不肖之身為先生之累哉。

translations.literal: Otherwise, how would he dare to burden the Master with an unworthy person such as himself?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how would he dare to burden the Master with an unworthy person such as himself?

sentences.zh: 從之累年，授《春秋》、《中庸》、《語》、《孟》之說。

translations.literal: He followed him for years; Congyan taught him the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Mean, the Analects, and the Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: He followed him for years; Congyan taught him the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Mean, the Analects, and the Mencius.

sentences.zh: 從彥好靜坐，侗退入室中，亦靜坐。

translations.literal: Congyan liked sitting in quiet meditation; when Tong withdrew into the inner room, he too sat in quiet meditation.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan liked sitting in quiet meditation; when Tong withdrew into the inner room, he too sat in quiet meditation.

sentences.zh: 從彥令靜中看喜怒哀樂未發前氣象，而求所謂「中」者，久之，而於天下之理該攝洞貫，以次融釋，各有條序，從彥亟稱許焉。

translations.literal: Congyan had him in quiet meditation observe the atmosphere before joy, anger, sorrow, and delight had issued forth and seek what is called the Mean; after a long time, he comprehensively grasped and penetrated the principles of all under Heaven, melting and releasing them in sequence, each with its order; Congyan greatly praised and approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan had him in quiet meditation observe the atmosphere before joy, anger, sorrow, and delight had issued forth and seek what is called the Mean. After a long time, he comprehensively grasped and penetrated the principles of all under Heaven, melting and releasing them in sequence, each with its order; Congyan greatly praised and approved him.

sentences.zh: 既而退居山田，謝絕世故余四十年，食飲或不充，而怡然自適。

translations.literal: Before long he retired to live in the mountain fields, declining worldly affairs for more than forty years; sometimes food and drink were insufficient, yet he was content and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired to live in the mountain fields, declining worldly affairs for more than forty years. Sometimes food and drink were insufficient, yet he was content and at ease.

sentences.zh: 事親孝謹，仲兄性剛多忤，侗事之得其歡心。

translations.literal: In serving his parents he was filial and careful; his second elder brother was by nature stern and often contentious, yet Tong served him and won his delight.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his parents he was filial and careful. His second elder brother was by nature stern and often contentious, yet Tong served him and won his delight.

sentences.zh: 閨門內外，夷愉肅穆，若無人聲，而眾事自理。

translations.literal: Within the inner and outer quarters, all was easy and pleasant, solemn and respectful, as if no human voice were heard, yet the multitude of affairs was self-regulated.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner and outer quarters, all was easy and pleasant, solemn and respectful, as if no human voice were heard, yet the multitude of affairs was self-regulated.

sentences.zh: 親戚有貧不能婚嫁者，則為經理振助之。

translations.literal: When relatives were too poor to marry off their sons or daughters, he would manage and assist them.
translations.idiomatic: When relatives were too poor to marry off their sons or daughters, he would manage and assist them.

sentences.zh: 與鄉人處，飲食言笑，終日油油如也。

translations.literal: In dealing with fellow villagers, in eating, drinking, speaking, and laughing, all day he was easy and unhurried.
translations.idiomatic: In dealing with fellow villagers, in eating, drinking, speaking, and laughing, all day he was easy and unhurried.

sentences.zh: 其接後學，答問不倦，雖隨人淺深施教，而必自反身自得始。

translations.literal: In receiving later students, he answered questions without weariness; though he taught according to each person's depth, he always began by turning back to obtain it in oneself.
translations.idiomatic: In receiving later students, he answered questions without weariness. Though he taught according to each person's depth, he always began by turning back to obtain it in oneself.

sentences.zh: 故其言曰：「學問之道不在多言，但默坐澄心，體認天理。

translations.literal: Therefore his words were: "The Way of learning is not in speaking much; only sit quietly and clarify the heart, embodying and recognizing Heavenly principle.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore his words were, "The Way of learning is not in speaking much; only sit quietly and clarify the heart, embodying and recognizing Heavenly principle.

sentences.zh: 若是，雖一毫私慾之發，亦退聽矣。」

translations.literal: If so, even when the slightest private desire arises, it will withdraw and listen."
translations.idiomatic: If so, even when the slightest private desire arises, it will withdraw and listen."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「學者之病，在於未有灑然冰解凍釋處。

translations.literal: He also said: "The illness of learners lies in not yet having a place where things melt like ice thawing and frost releasing.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The illness of learners lies in not yet having a place where things melt like ice thawing and frost releasing.

sentences.zh: 如孔門諸子，群居終日，交相切磨，又得夫子為之依歸，日用之間觀感而化者多矣。

translations.literal: Like the disciples at Confucius's gate, living together all day and mutually cutting and polishing, moreover obtaining the Master as their reliance—in daily use, those who observed and were transformed by contact were many.
translations.idiomatic: Like the disciples at Confucius's gate, living together all day and mutually cutting and polishing, moreover obtaining the Master as their reliance—in daily use, those who observed and were transformed by contact were many.

sentences.zh: 恐於融釋而不脫落處，非言說所及也。」

translations.literal: I fear that at the place of melting and releasing but not yet falling free, speech cannot reach."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that at the place of melting and releasing but not yet falling free, speech cannot reach."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「讀書者知其所言莫非吾事，而即吾身以求之，則凡聖賢所至而吾所未至者，皆可勉而進矣。

translations.literal: He also said: "Readers who know that what is spoken is none other than our own affair, and seek it in their own persons, then whatever the sages and worthies reached and we have not yet reached—all can be exerted toward and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Readers who know that what is spoken is none other than our own affair, and seek it in their own persons, then whatever the sages and worthies reached and we have not yet reached—all can be exerted toward and advanced.

sentences.zh: 若直求之文字，以資誦說，其不為玩物喪志者幾希。」

translations.literal: If one directly seeks it in the written text to supply recitation and exposition, there are few who will not treat it as plaything and lose their will."
translations.idiomatic: If one directly seeks it in the written text to supply recitation and exposition, there are few who will not treat it as plaything and lose their will."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「講學切在深潛縝密，然後氣味深長，蹊徑不差。

translations.literal: He also said: "Lecturing and learning must cut deeply, sink quietly, and be dense and fine; only then is the flavor deep and long and the path without error.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Lecturing and learning must cut deeply, sink quietly, and be dense and fine; only then is the flavor deep and long and the path without error.

sentences.zh: 若概以理一，而不察其分之殊，此學者所以流於疑似亂真之說而不自知也。」

translations.literal: If one broadly takes principle as one without examining the differences of its manifestations, this is how learners flow into doubtful doctrines that confuse the true without knowing it themselves."
translations.idiomatic: If one broadly takes principle as one without examining the differences of its manifestations, this is how learners flow into doubtful doctrines that confuse the true without knowing it themselves."

sentences.zh: 嘗以黃庭堅之稱濂溪周茂叔「胸中酒落，如光風霽月」，為善形容有道者氣象，嘗諷誦之，而顧謂學者存此於胸中，庶幾遇事廓然，而義理少進矣。

translations.literal: He once took Huang Tingjian's praise of Zhou Maoshu of Lianxi—"in his breast free and unbound, like bright wind after rain clears the moon"—as a fine description of the atmosphere of one who has the Way; he often chanted it in recitation and turned to tell learners to preserve this in the breast, so that perhaps when affairs arise they will be open and clear and principle will advance somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He once took Huang Tingjian's praise of Zhou Maoshu of Lianxi—"in his breast free and unbound, like bright wind after rain clears the moon"—as a fine description of the atmosphere of one who has the Way. He often chanted it in recitation and turned to tell learners to preserve this in the breast, so that perhaps when affairs arise they will be open and clear and principle will advance somewhat.

sentences.zh: 其語《中庸》曰：「聖門之傳是書，其所以開悟後學無遺策矣。

translations.literal: In speaking of the Mean he said: "The sage gate's transmission of this book is such that in awakening later learners there is no strategy left out.
translations.idiomatic: In speaking of the Mean he said, "The sage gate's transmission of this book is such that in awakening later learners there is no strategy left out.

sentences.zh: 然所謂『喜怒哀樂未發謂之中』者，又一篇之指要也。

translations.literal: Yet what is called 'before joy, anger, sorrow, and delight issue forth is called the Mean' is again the essential point of the whole piece.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what is called 'before joy, anger, sorrow, and delight issue forth is called the Mean' is again the essential point of the whole piece.

sentences.zh: 若徒記誦而已，則亦奚以為哉？

translations.literal: If one merely memorizes and recites, then of what use is it?
translations.idiomatic: If one merely memorizes and recites, then of what use is it?

sentences.zh: 必也體之於身，實見是理，若顏子之歎，卓然若有所見，而不違乎心目之間，然後擴充而往，無所不通，則庶乎其可以言《中庸》矣。」

translations.literal: One must embody it in the person and truly see this principle, like Yan Hui's sigh—standing out as though he had seen something and not violating what is between the eyes and heart—only then expanding and proceeding, nothing blocked; then perhaps one can speak of the Mean."
translations.idiomatic: One must embody it in the person and truly see this principle, like Yan Hui's sigh—standing out as though he had seen something and not violating what is between the eyes and heart—only then expanding and proceeding, nothing blocked; then perhaps one can speak of the Mean."

sentences.zh: 其語《春秋》曰：「《春秋》一事各是發明一例，如觀山水，徙步而形勢不同，不可拘以一法。

translations.literal: In speaking of the Spring and Autumn Annals he said: "In the Spring and Autumn, each event illuminates one example; it is like viewing mountains and waters—as one walks the forms and situations differ and cannot be confined to one method.
translations.idiomatic: In speaking of the Spring and Autumn Annals he said, "In the Spring and Autumn, each event illuminates one example; it is like viewing mountains and waters—as one walks the forms and situations differ and cannot be confined to one method.

sentences.zh: 然所以難言者，蓋以常人之心推測聖人，未到聖人灑然處，豈能無失耶？」

translations.literal: Yet what makes it hard to speak of is that common men's hearts measure the sage; having not reached the sage's place of free release, how can one be without error?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet what makes it hard to speak of is that common men's hearts measure the sage. Having not reached the sage's place of free release, how can one be without error?"

sentences.zh: 侗既閒居，若無意當世，而傷時憂國，論事感激動人。

translations.literal: After Tong had retired to leisure, as if he had no intent toward the age, yet grieving at the times and worrying for the state, when he discussed affairs his emotion moved men.
translations.idiomatic: After Tong had retired to leisure, as if he had no intent toward the age, yet grieving at the times and worrying for the state, when he discussed affairs his emotion moved men.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「今日三綱不振，義利不分。

translations.literal: He once said: "Today the Three Bonds are not upheld and righteousness and profit are not distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Today the Three Bonds are not upheld and righteousness and profit are not distinguished.

sentences.zh: 三綱不振，故人心邪僻，不堪任用，是致上下之氣間隔，而中國日衰。

translations.literal: When the Three Bonds are not upheld, people's hearts are perverse and cannot be employed, causing the qi between above and below to be blocked and China daily to decline.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Bonds are not upheld, people's hearts are perverse and cannot be employed, causing the qi between above and below to be blocked and China daily to decline.

sentences.zh: 義利不分，故自王安石用事，陷溺人心，至今不自知覺。

translations.literal: When righteousness and profit are not distinguished, from the time Wang Anshi held power he drowned men's hearts, and to this day they do not know it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When righteousness and profit are not distinguished, from the time Wang Anshi held power he drowned men's hearts, and to this day they do not know it themselves.

sentences.zh: 人趨利而不知義，則主勢日孤，人主當於此留意，不然，則是所謂『雖有粟，吾得而食諸』也。」

translations.literal: When men rush to profit and do not know righteousness, the sovereign's position daily grows isolated; the sovereign should take note of this—otherwise it is what is called 'though there be grain, can I obtain it and eat?'"
translations.idiomatic: When men rush to profit and do not know righteousness, the sovereign's position daily grows isolated. The sovereign should take note of this—otherwise it is what is called 'though there be grain, can I obtain it and eat?'"

sentences.zh: 是時吏部員外郎朱松與侗為同門友，雅重侗，遣子熹從學，熹卒得其傳。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Zhu Song was Tong's fellow student and deeply esteemed him; he sent his son Xi to study, and Xi ultimately obtained his transmission.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Zhu Song was Tong's fellow student and deeply esteemed him. He sent his son Xi to study, and Xi ultimately obtained his transmission.

sentences.zh: 沙縣鄧迪嘗謂松曰：「願中如冰壺秋月，瑩徹無瑕，非吾曹所及。」

translations.literal: Deng Di of Shaxian once told Song: "Yuanzhong is like an ice pot and autumn moon, lucid and without flaw—not something we can match."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Di of Shaxian once told Song, "Yuanzhong is like an ice pot and autumn moon, lucid and without flaw—not something we can match."

sentences.zh: 松以謂知言。

translations.literal: Song considered this knowing speech.
translations.idiomatic: Song considered this knowing speech.

sentences.zh: 而熹亦稱同：「姿稟勁特，氣節豪邁，而充養完粹，無復圭角，精純之氣達於面目，色溫言厲，神定氣和，語默動靜，端詳閒泰，自然之中若有成法。

translations.literal: Xi also praised him similarly: "Endowment stern and special, spirit and integrity bold and expansive, yet cultivation complete and pure with no remaining sharp corners; the refined and pure qi reaches the face and countenance; complexion warm and words stern, spirit settled and qi harmonious; in speech and silence, movement and stillness, dignified, detailed, leisurely, and at ease—within naturalness there seems to be a formed method.
translations.idiomatic: Xi also praised him similarly: "Endowment stern and special, spirit and integrity bold and expansive, yet cultivation complete and pure with no remaining sharp corners. The refined and pure qi reaches the face and countenance; complexion warm and words stern, spirit settled and qi harmonious. In speech and silence, movement and stillness, dignified, detailed, leisurely, and at ease—within naturalness there seems to be a formed method.

sentences.zh: 平日恂恂，於事若無甚可否，及其酬酢事變，斷以義理，則有截然不可犯者。」

translations.literal: Daily he was respectful and agreeable; in affairs he seemed to approve or disapprove little; yet when responding to changing affairs and deciding by principle and righteousness, there was what was decisively not to be violated."
translations.idiomatic: Daily he was respectful and agreeable; in affairs he seemed to approve or disapprove little. Yet when responding to changing affairs and deciding by principle and righteousness, there was what was decisively not to be violated."

sentences.zh: 又謂自從侗學，辭去復來，則所聞益超絕。

translations.literal: He also said that from studying under Tong, departing and returning again, what he heard was ever more surpassing.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that from studying under Tong, departing and returning again, what he heard was ever more surpassing.

sentences.zh: 其上達不已如此。

translations.literal: His upward progress without ceasing was like this.
translations.idiomatic: His upward progress without ceasing was like this.

sentences.zh: 侗子友直、信甫皆舉進士，試吏旁郡，更請迎養。

translations.literal: Tong's sons Youzhi and Xinfu both passed the jinshi examination and served as officials in neighboring commanderies; they repeatedly requested to bring their parents to live with them.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's sons Youzhi and Xinfu both passed the jinshi examination and served as officials in neighboring commanderies; they repeatedly requested to bring their parents to live with them.

sentences.zh: 歸道武夷，會閩帥汪應辰以書幣來迎，侗往見之，至之日疾作，遂卒，年七十有一。

translations.literal: Returning by way of Wuyi, it happened that the Fujian commander Wang Yingchen sent letters and gifts to welcome him; Tong went to see him, and on the day he arrived illness seized him and he died, at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: Returning by way of Wuyi, it happened that the Fujian commander Wang Yingchen sent letters and gifts to welcome him. Tong went to see him, and on the day he arrived illness seized him and he died, at age seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 信甫仕至監察御史，出知衢州，擢廣東、江東憲，以特立不容於朝雲。

translations.literal: Xinfu served up to Supervising Censor, went out as prefect of Quzhou, was promoted to inspector of Guangdong and Jiangdong, and because of his upright independence was not tolerated at court.
translations.idiomatic: Xinfu served up to supervising censor, went out as prefect of Quzhou, was promoted to inspector of Guangdong and Jiangdong, and because of his upright independence was not tolerated at court.
